[Exclusive] SK hynix Begins Groundwork on Japan Fab

SK hynix has begun construction work for a memory semiconductor fab in Japan, just one month after the company said "nothing has been decided."

According to industry sources on the 28th, SK hynix has reportedly started groundwork for a semiconductor fab in Japan's Tohoku region. "It's unclear whether it will be a standalone fab or a joint venture with Kioxia, but it's true that foundation work is underway on site," an industry source said. "It shows how strongly SK hynix wants to enter the Japanese market."

The source added, "SK hynix has recently been asking domestic component suppliers to expand supply volumes. It's a sign the company is moving aggressively to respond to the memory supply shortage."

As recently as a month ago, SK hynix said a memory fab in Japan was "under review" and that "nothing specific has been decided." If true, the company moved at remarkable speed, beginning site preparation within a single month.

The Tohoku region is a major cluster for Japan's semiconductor and electronic components industries, with Iwate Prefecture at its core. Iwate hosts the Kitakami fab of Kioxia, a leading NAND flash maker, along with Japan Semiconductor, which makes microcontrollers (MCUs) and power MOSFETs, and Amkor Technology, which handles back end processing. Auto parts maker Denso and global chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron also have operations there. Adding the SK hynix memory fab now under construction would give the region a memory ecosystem spanning front end to back end processes.

This is also why Tohoku emerged as a leading candidate after SK Group Chairman Chey Tae Won said in August that the group was considering a joint memory fab in Japan. At the time, Chey said SK was "considering anywhere with abundant power and water," which further raised the odds of a move into Tohoku. Iwate in particular is known for excellent water infrastructure, given the concentration of semiconductor companies there.

If SK hynix builds a fab in Tohoku, Japan will complete a semiconductor triangle alongside TSMC in Kyushu and homegrown foundry Rapidus in Hokkaido, effectively linking the entire country through the semiconductor industry.

Meanwhile, SK hynix maintains that nothing has been decided yet. "The Japan memory fab is currently under review," a company official said. "Nothing has progressed beyond that."

author: nekuda_ai
quoted_text:
Hearing this week that personal assistants cost $3k-$7k per user per year, depending on scale effects / vertical integration / model selection. Implications/questions:

- Consumer subsidies will be a huge factor; people don’t care about privacy, they want utility and they want it for free.
- Model costs are deflating, but not fast enough for many startups. The dark horse is that Jev may rapidly deflate computer-use costs 100x.
- An interesting counter-position would be building an expensive and narrowly focused agent — perhaps combining proprietary supply (Carbone tables!) with a unique POV (“no one goes there anymore, go to The Grill instead”).
- Social is wide open but hinges on a key design challenge: how can agents increase social cohesion and not feel invasive in a group chat? A working social agent would rightly attract an avalanche of capital and be hard for incumbents to replicate.
- Finally, there are vertical focus areas like financial services where the LTVs outweigh the subsidy needed and are outside the near-term competitive focus of the incumbents. If it were me, I’d focus here — Credit Karma as an agent >> Credit Karma as an app.

Overall, it’s still very, very early, and we may very well be in the MySpace era of social or iPhone 2010. Hang onto your hats and keep building!!

🚨 Bitget lên tiếng sau sự cố an ninh: Cam kết minh bạch, tài sản người dùng được đảm bảo an toàn

Sàn giao dịch Bitget vừa chính thức lên tiếng về sự cố an ninh xảy ra trong đêm, khiến khoảng 351,6 triệu USD bị ảnh hưởng. Trước sự việc này, CEO Gracy Chen đã đại diện sàn đưa ra thông điệp trấn an cùng loạt cam kết cụ thể tới người dùng và đối tác.

1️⃣ Cam kết minh bạch, không né tránh sự cố

Bà Gracy Chen khẳng định Bitget không né tránh trách nhiệm trước sự cố lần này. Toàn bộ các khoản tiền bị ảnh hưởng cũng như mọi quyết định xử lý sẽ được sàn giải trình một cách minh bạch, rõ ràng tới cộng đồng người dùng.

2️⃣ Tài sản khách hàng được đảm bảo

Theo Bitget, sự cố tác động đến ví nóng (hot wallet) và ví ấm (warm wallet), trong khi ví lạnh (cold wallet) - nơi lưu trữ tài sản ngoại tuyến - vẫn được đảm bảo an toàn tuyệt đối. Số dư và tài sản của khách hàng được bảo vệ nguyên vẹn, không bị ảnh hưởng.

3️⃣ Quỹ Bảo vệ Người dùng đủ sức chi trả toàn bộ thiệt hại

Về phương án khắc phục, Bitget cho biết Quỹ Bảo vệ Người dùng (User Protection Fund) hiện có hơn 464 triệu USD, đủ để chi trả toàn bộ khoản thiệt hại ước tính 351,6 triệu USD. Đây là quỹ được sàn chuẩn bị sẵn nhằm ứng phó với chính những tình huống như vậy, giúp bảo vệ quyền lợi người dùng trong mọi trường hợp.

4️⃣ Xử lý khẩn cấp và cảnh báo an toàn cho người dùng

Hiện Bitget đã kích hoạt quy trình ứng phó khẩn cấp và phối hợp cùng các bên liên quan để xử lý sự cố. Song song đó, sàn cũng đưa ra cảnh báo quan trọng: người dùng tuyệt đối không cung cấp mật khẩu, mã xác thực hai lớp (2FA) hay cụm từ khôi phục ví (seed phrase) cho bất kỳ ai; đồng thời cảnh giác với những đối tượng tự nhận là bộ phận hỗ trợ để "giúp lấy lại tài sản".

5️⃣ Về hoạt động giao dịch

Tính năng nạp tiền và giao dịch trên sàn vẫn diễn ra bình thường. Riêng chức năng rút tiền được tạm ngưng như một biện pháp thận trọng, nhằm phục vụ quá trình rà soát và củng cố an ninh hệ thống.

text:
DeFi still treats almost every wallet like a stranger.

If you want credit, the default answer is usually simple:
overcollateralize.

That works, but it also shows how little context onchain finance has about the borrower.

ZKredit is one of the more interesting directions from @primus_labs with @BNBCHAIN and @brevis_zk.

The idea is to bring offchain financial reputation onchain without forcing users to expose the raw data behind it.

Instead of uploading your full exchange history or doxxing your financial profile, you prove specific claims:
account age, balance thresholds, activity history, credit-related signals.

Primus zkTLS verifies that the data came from the real source.

Brevis helps turn that into a proof that can actually be used onchain.

That matters because better credit rails need more than transparency.
They need context.

If DeFi wants to move beyond treating every borrower the same, privacy-preserving verification feels like one of the missing pieces.

The difficulty of asking questions on forums and StackOverflow drove people to reddit. The same forces of scale and moderation stressed reddit, so niche communities moved to private Discords. At every step information became more proprietary and less discoverable.

In 2023 all existing web content was scraped to bring about modern LLMs. AI finally allowed users to get the answer to any question with infinite patience, searching and synthesizing all possible public information. Google's AI answers atop search results were at first useless, but eventually got good enough to prevent you ever having to click on a hyperlink.

The result is a one-way interaction in which information value is extracted, but never added back into to the system.

The only way for someone passionate to supply the world valuable information about some hobby like vintage sewing machines is to willfully go back to r slash sewing machine enthusiasts and do eternal battle with moderators seeking to be the king of their little hill on one side and the onslaught of competing AI/normie slop on the other.

text:
Claude can help you build a game.

Give it access to Unreal Engine, Blender, and game-development skills, and you can go a lot further.

Here are 7 GitHub repos worth saving if you want to build games with AI.

Use them with a coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex, following each repo’s setup instructions.

1/ Awesome Gamedev Agent Skills

A collection of 73 skills covering Unity, Unreal, Godot, browser games, and more.

It gives your agent guidance for tasks like building an inventory, adding enemy behavior, creating save files, and making movement feel responsive.

The useful part: it picks relevant skills based on your engine and what you ask for.

Start here if your AI keeps producing code that ignores how your game actually works.

https://t.co/WudWTsajr7

2/ Three.js Game Skills

For building 3D games people can open in their browser.

Nine skills cover gameplay, graphics, menus, audio, assets, debugging, and release checks.

It includes a starter project and browser-testing templates. The README also links to playable demos, including a drifting game and a space dogfight.

Install it, then ask your agent to use “threejs-game-director” to build your idea.

https://t.co/OkZpJhvKnV

3/ Unreal MCP

Connects an AI assistant to Unreal Engine.

It exposes tools for placing objects, editing materials, working with Blueprints, adjusting lighting, creating particle effects, and controlling cinematic sequences.

A useful starting task: block out one small level, place the camera, and set up the lighting.

This requires Unreal and the repo’s plugin setup.

https://t.co/1dGWbYeSAW

4/ MCP for Unity

Gives your AI tools to work inside the Unity Editor.

It can create scenes and objects, edit C# scripts, manage assets, run tests, and build the project.

That gives you a workflow where the agent can make changes and check them inside the engine.

Useful for turning individual features into a playable prototype.

https://t.co/go63szyvru

5/ Godot MCP

Connects your AI agent to Godot.

It can create scenes, add objects, load sprites, launch the game, and read error messages.

That last part matters. When something breaks, the agent can inspect the actual error and work on a fix.

A good option for building a small game around one clear mechanic.

https://t.co/qXwHTtguqL

6/ MCP for Blender

For creating and changing the 3D objects that go into your game.

Connect it to Blender, then ask your AI to create objects, adjust materials, and arrange scenes.

It also supports asset sources including Poly Haven and Sketchfab, plus optional AI model-generation services.

Think props, buildings, furniture, and environment pieces. Check asset licenses and any external service costs.

https://t.co/n1xKro20HB

7/ Agentic Gamedev Skills

For the work that comes after “the game runs.”

This collection focuses on mini-games, with workflows for testing mechanics, tuning difficulty, adding sound, improving impact feedback, and catching browser crashes.

Useful when your prototype works but jumping feels weak, the rules are confusing, or one cheap trick wins every time.

https://t.co/wx8b2PRU3f

My suggestion: pick one engine, add the relevant skills, and build one small playable level.

Try this prompt:

“Build a five-minute playable demo of [idea]. Use the installed game-development skills and connected tools. Start with movement, camera, one core mechanic, and a clear win or lose condition. Run it and fix errors before adding more features. Then improve lighting, sound, feedback, and performance. Tell me what still needs human testing.”

AAA-quality work still takes art direction, good assets, optimization, and a lot of testing. No repo guarantees that.

But you can start with one room, one enemy, and one mechanic worth playing again.

What game have you wanted to build for years?

Nubank and Guardrails AI just published a playbook for safely supercharging customer-support LLM agents—without risking real customer trust.

Their SNOWGLOBE simulator lets “synthetic customers” stress-test agents at the tool interface, generating thousands of persona-driven chats in minutes. No live users exposed, no backend touched.

Results: simulation speeds iteration 4.8×, and improvements guided by this layer boosted self-service rate by +4.9 pp and transactional NPS by +36.7 in live A/B tests. Screening 29 open-weight models, they picked a Qwen-3.5 config that upped SSR another +8.8 pp and cut p95 latency 25%, all with no tNPS drop.

The takeaway: you can now explore prompts, models, even edge-case policies safely and at scale—transforming how banks, e-commerce, and telcos build and launch support bots.

🗡️ What DeFi Shipped 🚢 (Sept 25):

Nasdaq approved Pyth to distribute its stock-price data, Ondo added a way to tokenize existing shares, and Hyperliquid switched on borrowing.

Here’s how those work, plus 7 more updates worth catching up on:

• @HyperliquidX turned on manual borrows. You can now post HYPE or BTC as collateral and borrow USDC or USDT, with rates set by utilization.

• @Ondo now lets approved institutions mint Ondo Stocks with shares they already hold, through @AlpacaHQ's Instant Tokenization Network. It's live on Ethereum and @BNBCHAIN.

• @PythNetwork won Nasdaq approval to redistribute Nasdaq Basic through its data feeds. That puts licensed US equity prices on the same rails as its crypto feeds.

• @Polymarket hired Zora's former CEO Jacob Horne to "make Polymarket DeFi great again." @shayne_coplan admits the onchain product has waned while the team focused on the US.

• @zetachain holders voted to migrate ZETA to Solana, with 99.4% in favor. The team is folding its L1 and betting everything on @anumaai, its private AI app.

• @stablecoin_x's 48-month lock-up on its ENA is permanently waived from October 5. Its stack is ~3.03B ENA, about 20% of supply, although any sale still needs @ethena Foundation consent.

• @variational_io says its $VAR TGE will occur in Q4 2026, with 32% of the total supply airdropped to users based on Variational points.

• @jumperapp is getting a token. solana:Aybt5BWuW6kMNt7Jk1UmSgLzpEKev5pEnh82TA5rpump was announced days after a perps waitlist went up.

• @Trueo_ is moving its prediction market from @base to Ethereum mainnet, pointing to deeper integrations and its next oracle system. TRUE holders can migrate with no deadline.

• @longdotxyz says it will act as an incubator, not a launcher, working with top stock-pair teams to build their own moats. Stricter "PVE" protections like ticker locks are coming too.

An L1 voted itself out of existence, and a prediction market is leaving Base for Ethereum mainnet. 

Nobody's loyal to infrastructure anymore, esp when it's so easy to bridge and shift tokens around. 

They go wherever the users and the liquidity already are.

quoted_text:
从 Bybit 到 Bitget： THORChain 为何屡屡沦为黑客的“完美洗钱出口”？

据统计，2023 到 2026 年间，经 THORChain 处理的已知非法资金高达 92.7 亿美元，协议与节点从中赚取了超过 1200 万美元的手续费。

2026 年 9 月 26 日，Bitget 平台约 3.875 亿美元资金遭黑客洗劫。随着链上追踪显示黑客正将上亿美元的 XRP、BNB 等赃款送入 @THORChain 兑换为难以追回的原生 BTC，Bitget CEO @GracyBitget  在 X 平台正式向 THORChain 发起质问：“去中心化是设计原则，不是给已知赃款开绿灯的挡箭牌。”

面对指责，THORChain 给出的回应依然强硬：协议与比特币、以太坊一样，是无需许可的网络，无权也不该扮演执法角色的审查者。

然而，伴随着黑客兑换带来的爆棚手续费收入，RUNE 价格与成交量应声大涨。一方面是受害者与行业安全机构的怒火，另一方面是协议收入与代币价格的无情狂欢——THORChain 再次被推到了公义与中立性交锋的风口浪尖。

1️⃣ 无包装跨链：洗钱天堂的“完美出口”

黑客为何如此偏爱 THORChain？答案在于其独特的机制设计。

普通的跨链桥往往需要将资产包装为映射代币（如 WETH、USDC），而背后的发行方（如 Circle、Tether）拥有黑名单和冻结能力。但 THORChain 实现了原生资产的无包装互换，攻击者入场，直接换成毫无中心化控制权的原生 BTC。

从 2025 年 Bybit 14 亿美金大案（约 12 亿美元经此洗走），到 2026 年 4 月 KelpDAO 案（1.75 亿美元经此跨链），再到如今的 Bitget 事件，据统计，2023 至 2026 年间已有超 90 亿美元的非法交易量流经 THORChain，为协议和流动性提供者（LP）贡献了过千万美元的手续费。

每当行业遭遇浩劫，THORChain 的手续费盘子就极其讽刺地吃饱一次。

2️⃣ 所谓的“无法干预”：是能力不足，还是治理意愿？

THORChain 官方将自己媲美为比特币和以太坊，自称“无权干涉”。但这套说法在业内权威安全专家和交易所创始人眼中，完全站不住脚。

OKX 创始人 @star_okx 犀利指出：“TSS（阈值签名）把控制权分给多方，把中介分散，并不等于消灭了中介。” 比特币没有任何一个委员会可以开会决定“先停机一下”，但 THORChain 有。

链上历史证据更是给这种“无法干预”打上了巨大的问号：

· 2021 年连遭攻击：节点快速反应，隔离、停交易、修路由再重启。
· 2026 年 5 月“自盗”事件：恶意节点抽走 1070 万美元，官方自动检测加人工投票，瞬间停机 39 天重新修复。
· 2025 年 Bybit 案：3 名验证者曾投票暂停 ETH 交易拦截朝鲜黑客，但几分钟内被另外 4 票推翻，主开发者 Pluto 甚至因不满这种“选择性不拦截”而愤然离职。

正如慢雾余弦所质问：为什么自身金库被掏时，协议可以迅速停机 39 天；而当行业发生巨额黑客大案、全网地址标定清晰时，却改口“无权干涉”，继续大肆抽取黑客贡献的手续费？

这证明了一点：THORChain 拦截赃款的技术能力一直都在，缺少的只是治理意愿。

3️⃣ 去中心化不该是吸血的挡箭牌

去中心化和抗审查无疑是 Web3 最核心的基石与信仰。然而，当一个协议在利益面前表现出“对我有利时我是无需许可的基础设施，涉及到我损失时我就是有权限控制的软件”时，它所展现的就不是对去中心化信念的坚守，而是裸的选择性双标。

跨链协议卡在了便捷与合规的缝隙里。对于 RUNE 的持有者而言，黑客兑换带来的短期成交脉冲固然养眼，但长期来看，被全行业公认沦为黑灰产“洗钱出货终端”的合规代价与声誉反噬，终究需要在同一张账单上加倍偿还。

链上实现价值可以视为所有实际流向BTC的资金（只要上链）。如图，当前走出熊底的三段式结构和2023年非常相似。

第1段，资本从“大幅流出”到“减缓流出”；
第2段，资本从“净流出”转为“净流入”，第一波启动。
第3段，资本保持净流入，但开始和价格形成背离。

目前我们正处于“第3段”。而2023年3段走完就迎来了一次“像样”的回调，深度直达STH-RP。

经历过的小伙伴应该记得，当时还叠加了几个外部因素，包括：宏观利率预期变鹰、加密友好银行暴雷等。

本轮是否会完全复刻？我们不得而知。

不过，只要资金和价格背离持续存在，越到后面动能越弱。直到下一波强劲的资本流入，来打破这种格局。

text:
Perp 积分又热起来了，聊一下我的看法。

@variational_io  我在极早期参与了，当时邀请码非常难。去年因为主要研究 @Lighter_xyz ，所以我的VAR积分主要是溯源积分。

其实今年测算过成本，当时评估了一下赔率相对不高，就没有重点farm了，不过也有参与，正常使用，算是持续跟进优质的项目。

 今年下半年没有想到  HYPE 和 LIT 如此强势，直接进一步催化了VAR的积分价值。

现在有点半场开香槟的感觉。多年的farm经验，让我感觉有点谨慎。

VAR 是个优秀的潜力项目，但是短期期间仍然要依赖于HYPE LIT打开的市场上限。我不能因为我自己持有积分就狂热看多，这样的教训太多了。保持理性，客观。

VAR之后，该去哪里？

首先考虑的不应该是该farm哪个项目，因为还有一个更靠前的问题：perp 市场是否还有红利空间，市场还能再支撑几个市值超过10B的项目。这个问题更关键。

我更偏向于空间上限依然巨大，存量空间有限。

说人话，长期看来，优质的perpdex依然有巨大的空间，hype 依然也被低估，市场依旧需要方便好用的perp平台。

举个例子，HYPE 的市值为 900亿，如果还有龙二，他的市值至少100亿很正常，考虑到并不在竞争末期，龙二在500亿美元左右的市值也不算离谱，这说明一件事情，龙头确定，龙二的空间依旧很大，甚至谁是龙二还没有确定下来。因为数据上面还没有断崖式的领先。

况且，HYPE 还在超越某安的路上。

现在说但是。

上面的都是长期来看，而短期来看，竞争非常激烈。perp dex 今年的价格上来了，数据侧的增速并没有那么快。存量市场已经没有溢价了，谁能吸引更多的增量用户成为了关键。

回到上个问题，行业依然有空间，但是下一个选择谁？

其实现在很难看清，回到去年的时间线，HYPE 撑起了行业的天花板，第二，第三都会有溢价。这就是 LIT VAR 有空间快速发展的一个外在原因。

而下一个选择逻辑上就没有这么清晰了，我们或许只知道可能是更细分的专业化平台（ @entropyIO  ），或许可能承接RWA的交易平台（ @arcus_xyz  ），但都不敢这么确定最终获胜的是哪家，中途有没有更优秀的平台跑出来。

因为我们并不知道下一个叙事或新的玩法。我只知道链上交易平台始终是有空间。

如果cex仍然占行业的主体，更perp dex 仍然有溢价空间。

以时代性来看perpdex ，我觉得更合适。

我自己也会继续关注和farm我认为不错的平台，以投资之心，看错了就当学费了。

text:
Liquidation Heatmap 的實用性真的被高估太多了。

現在很多人看圖看到某個價位有一大片 liquidation cluster，就直接解讀成「價格一定會去掃這裡」。

但圖本身就有很多的假設成分。

大部分 Liquidation Heatmap 的做法，是根據市場上的成交歷史，套入一組假設的槓桿倍數，比如 5x、10x、20x、30x、50x，去反推出這些成交後的倉位「可能」在哪些價位被清算。

所以你看到的 liquidation cluster，並不代表那裡真的躺著一模一樣數量、等著被爆掉的倉位。

中間有太多變數了。

這些人可能早就 TP 了，也可能已經止損離場。

有人會加倉、有人會減倉，有人會補保證金，只要倉位大小、保證金或平均成本改變，liquidation price 就會跟著移動。

時間拉得越長，這種誤差就會越來越大。

所以 Liquidation Heatmap 最有參考價值的區間，大概就是最近 24 小時到 3 天。

再往上看到 7 天、30 天，甚至拿幾個幾個月前的 liquidation cluster 當成現在的「磁鐵價位」，就沒有任何意義了。

Liquidation Heatmap 可以拿來當短期市場結構的輔助資訊，但在交易體系中不應該佔太大成分，因為很容易產生一種假的確定性。

價格上下方，永遠都會有 liquidation cluster。

漲了，可以說是先掃上面的空單。
跌了，可以說是先掃下面的多單。

先跌再漲，可以說先掃多再掃空。
先漲再跌，也可以說先掃空再掃多。

怎麼走都有一套事後解釋。

無論市場怎麼走都能解釋，而且很難事前證偽，這就不是分析工具了，就是純玄學了。

text:
$LEVERAGE 915k dyor

BM2k8mJUbMthHoioykyUm2NjMrXvLBYhoXruwYLpump

okx wallet:https://t.co/67siMWjpZu

A leverage trading platform built specifically for the Pump ecosystem. Its core idea is to allow newly launched Meme coins to have perpetual futures markets from day one, supporting both long and short positions.

Users connect their Solana wallet, deposit SOL, and can open positions on Pump tokens with up to 5x leverage, either long or short.

Prices are sourced directly onchain, with no additional oracle.

Before opening a position, users can see the entry price, liquidation price, and maximum loss.

Anyone can fund a pool for a specific token to list a perpetual market for it, with the pool acting as the counterparty.

The liquidation engine checks every few seconds, and losses cannot exceed the margin.

Simply put, it’s basically adding a “mini Hyperliquid” layer to Pump’s Meme coins.

The platform also has several core design features:

Onchain pricing + single mark price:
Opening, closing, and liquidation all use the same onchain price, reducing disputes.
Creator Pool:
The project team or anyone else can fund a pool to list a market. The pool takes on the counterparty risk, and it cannot lose more than the amount of capital in the pool.

Fee flywheel:
A portion of creator fees is used to continuously buy back and immediately burn LEVERAGE, directly tying platform trading activity to token deflation.
The LEVERAGE token currently mainly serves as a mechanism for buybacks and burns, turning platform usage directly into deflationary pressure.

There's something poetic about recovery and asynchrony resilience being the largest clusters of lemmas here. You could say they are hard-earned!

Because what makes Ethereum's consensus one-of-a-kind is its ability to recover from faults while continuing to make progress ("dynamic availability"). And this turns these two properties, which are otherwise simple to obtain, into very subtle challenges.

So it doesn't come for free, and forces us to trade off on other dimensions like speed and simplicity. The complexity cost is very explicit on that plot!

But now this complexity cost is heavily amortised with a single (very long) mathematical proof that is computationally verifiable. There remains "only" the work of turning it into executable code.

For that, you should check out @asn_d6 and @kevaundray's latest on Ethereum's trusted computing base. Protocol design and engineering is now at a turning point.

author: KevinWSHPod
quoted_text:
$HYPE 已上线 Binance 现货交易。

去年5月，已上过 HYPE 的合约，当时流行的观点是不太可能会上现货，时隔一年之后还是格局了。

HYPE 当前市值已进入前十，昨天刚创过接近 98 美元的新高。

过去一年多，Hyperliquid 已经从 Binance 手里抢走了一部分专业交易员和追求自托管的资金，永续成交量占比从个位数升到双位数。

那么，忽略一个已经进入前十、成交活跃、社区极强的代币，等于把手续费和流量白白让给别人。

CEX 上 DEX 代币是行业常态，UNI、dYdX 当年也是这样。

以前 Binance 可以慢上、甚至不上直接竞对代币。现在市值到了这个级别，不上反而显得被动。

短期看对 HYPE 是种利好，但需要注意上币后也可能出现 sell the news 或套利盘。

但是，上币解决的是代币流通问题，两个交易所产品形态有本质差异。
一个要 KYC + 托管，一个完全链上 + 自托管，用户分层会继续存在。

上币对两家在永续合约上的竞争格局，影响没有想象中那么大。

author: james_x
quoted_text:
做了一个个人加密项目信息追踪工具，叫 Signal，已经开源，大家可以下载到自己的电脑上使用。（把github链接扔给agent就行）

做它的原因很简单。关注一个项目，消息往往散在官方账号、团队成员的推文和 KOL 的讨论里。看完这些，还得切到行情页面，确认价格和持仓量有没有变化。

Signal 把这些入口放进了一个按项目整理的中文阅读器。添加关注项目后，可以查看官方资讯、关联的团队账号，以及检索到的近期讨论者。内容优先显示中文，也能随时切回原文核对。

首页会整理上次访问后的未读更新，同一事件的相关报道放进时间线，方便跟进后续。项目页面还带有 K 线，可以设置价格、OI 和均线突破提醒。EMA 200／360 上穿支持选择 1 小时、4 小时或日线，按收盘确认。

工具运行在自己的电脑上，关注列表和阅读记录保存在本地。准备 Python 和自己的 @newsliquidX  API Token（最低每月2U就行），按仓库里的中文教程就能开始，不需要购买服务器。只使用阅读器，也不用安装 AI 助手或 skills。源码免费开源，数据接口可能产生费用。

目前是 Beta 版本，欢迎先拿几个自己关注的项目试用，遇到问题可以到 GitHub 提 Issue，记得去掉 Token 等私人信息。

罗永浩突然跑到 X 上，指责的那位郑刚，是紫辉创投创始人，当年锤子科技的早期投资人之一。

在锤子最困难的时候，郑刚的基金分两次借给公司 1500万，约定年利率 6%，后来锤子失败，双方在股权回购、借款、利息怎么算上产生严重分歧。

从 2023 年开始，双方就在微博上互相公开攻击，一直打到现在。

但这次最牛批的是，昨天晚间，紫辉创投创始人郑刚，发布实名举报，指控罗永浩及交个朋友（罗永浩之前搞卖货的那个直播间公司）涉嫌重大偷税漏税。

他说罗永浩利用自家亲戚和同事，罗永秀、黄贺及李钧等人的名义，注册了几十家空壳洗钱公司，存在重大偷税漏税。

但就在郑刚在韩国发帖的同时，还在微博上说 9 月 29 日要在韩国和当地机构，一起办一场投资交流活动。罗永浩看到后，直接用韩文在 X 上发了一封公开信，点名韩国高丽大学等。

说你们这次搞交流的对象郑刚，在中国是失信被执行人，如果韩方被骗了，他可以帮忙把情况，转交给中国媒体和执法部门。

另外他好奇，这老哥怎么在限高的同时，能坐飞机去韩国的，是不是偷渡。

撕的真狠，都跑到 X 上来了。

text:
如果你在做 Web3 产品，可以顺手给 Agent 接一套「新闻 + Twitter + 交易」能力。

最近看到几个不错的开源项目：

OpenNews MCP：实时新闻、AI 摘要、情绪分析、美股研报/财报电话会
OpenTwitter MCP：推文搜索、用户信息、KOL 追踪
OpenTrade：CEX/DEX/经纪商交易、持仓、代币分析、风控
Twitter → Binance Square：自动把 Twitter 内容同步到币安广场
Daily News：自动生成每日加密新闻摘要与市场分析

核心思路很简单：

别只给 Web3 应用接行情数据，也给它接“信息流”。

首页会整理上次访问后的未读更新，同一事件的相关报道放进时间线，方便跟进后续。项目页面还带有 K 线，可以设置价格、OI 和均线突破提醒。EMA 200／360 上穿支持选择 1 小时、4 小时或日线，按收盘确认。

quoted_text:
"放眼五年后，每个人都会拥有一个能深刻理解你的目标及周遭一切、并帮你搞定各种事务的智能体。"

这是马克·扎克伯格对未来五年的判断。9月25日，科技博主Jacklyn Dallas在Meta Connect大会前后专访扎克伯格。此时，个人智能体Muse上线两周，用户已达数百万。他第一次完整讲透Llama 4为何失败、Meta如何重组、眼镜与AI如何合流，以及"攻克所有疾病"的新时间表。想看懂Meta下一个十年，这是绕不开的一份文本。

01｜两周数百万，目标数十亿

"我们才推出两周，就有数百万人在使用它，这相当罕见。""每隔几年我们才会遇到这样的爆款。"看到早期原型时，他就下了判断："这注定会成为数十亿人渴望使用的产品。"

从数百万到数十亿，差的不是模型，是信任。

02｜AI也要懂分寸

 "如果你在构建Claude Code，你的模型不需要具备任何分寸感。"个人智能体不同：帮你订餐厅，不该泄露你的过敏史或怀孕。"这是一项特定技能，也是人类具备的基本社交技能或常识。"而Meta能做到，"因为我们做的是全栈开发"。 

编程智能体比的是智商，个人智能体比的是教养。

03｜每个智能体一台电脑

 "一个智能体要为你做事，就需要一个地方来存储你的信息，我们认为不应该把它和其他所有人的信息混在一个池子里。"Meta请来WhatsApp加密的合作者Moxie Marlinspike设计Muse Confidential VM，"我们甚至无法看到你虚拟机里的内容。" 

一家靠数据起家的公司，开始卖"我看不见你的数据"。

04｜技术树走反了 

"十或十五年前，我曾以为我们会先实现全息投影，然后才迎来高度发达的AI。"结果相反，"这完全出乎我的意料"。而眼镜，"是唯一一种能让设备与你同看、同听，全天候在你耳边交流，并最终显示图像的硬件形态"。 

被嘲笑多年的眼镜押注，意外成了AI最好的容器。

05｜2030：沙发上坐着AI 

他设想扑克之夜，"其中一半人物理在场，另外几个人通过全息投影加入并一起玩牌"。开会时，"也许沙发上还有几个空位，它们就可以作为全息投影出现在那里"。"这与Zoom通话之类的体验截然不同。" 未来的同事名单里，会有不占工位的成员。
06｜Llama 4错在组织 "我在团队的整体架构上犯了错。"他照搬了Instagram信息流和广告系统的模式，数百上千人并行。"你真正需要的是一个非常紧密的团队，把它当作一个集体科研项目来对待。""团队中的每一个席位都极其宝贵。" 

前沿模型拼的不是人数，是密度。

07｜不创造就焦躁

 "我觉得若不释放创造力、不去动手创造，我就会变得焦躁易怒。"在他看来，AI第一次拉低了创造的门槛："AI可以帮你勾勒出雏形，然后你再像雕琢雕塑一样不断打磨完善。你不需要在动手前就掌握所有细节。" 

过去创造靠天赋和资本，现在先靠一个念头。

08｜"本世纪末太长了" 

Biohub（扎克伯格和妻子普莉希拉·陈的生物医学研究机构）原本的目标是帮科学界在本世纪末攻克所有疾病，"这在当时颇具争议"。如今团队在构建虚拟细胞模型，最终可能模拟"整个生物体甚至完整的人"。"现在我认为本世纪末这个时间太长了。" 

当生物学可以被仿真，医学就进入了软件的速度。

09｜用算力硬闯AGI

 "只要能构建一个足够庞大的超级计算机集群，就可以通过庞大的算力强行突破并达到目标。"俄亥俄吉瓦级集群已基本运营，路易斯安那5吉瓦集群在建。人脑功耗仅约10瓦，但他认为，"即使需要耗资数千亿美元，也是完全值得的"。 

这不是科学信仰，是一张用资本对冲不确定性的保单。

10｜对齐是产品底线

 "如果用户让Muse智能体执行某项任务，它却做出了完全相反的举动，那还有多少人愿意使用它呢？"他强调对齐必须前移到训练阶段，"就像父母教育孩子一样，你需要设定明确的边界"。Muse为此多搁置了几个月。 

在扎克伯格的语境里，安全不是刹车，而是留存率。

从Llama 4的低谷，到Muse两周数百万用户，Meta用了大约一年。答案不是更多人，而是更紧的团队、自研全栈、每人一台加密电脑和吉瓦级算力。元宇宙、眼镜、大模型，三场被看衰的豪赌，最终拼成同一件产品：个人超级智能。五年后，那个"深刻理解你"的智能体未必来自Meta，但门票已经写明：信任，比算力更难扩展。

如果每个人都会有一个比自己更懂自己的AI，你愿意把它托管在谁的服务器上？

text:
最近看到 Cursor 团队分享的一份 Agent Harness Token 优化 Prompt，挺值得收藏。

目标很直接，任务质量不降，同时把每个完整任务的成本压下来。一轮优化后，他们的整体 Token 成本降低了约 7%。

我觉得最值得学的是，他们把优化单位放在了完整任务上。

Agent 每一轮都要重新带上 Prompt、Tools、Context 和历史记录。单次请求看起来省了 Token，如果因此多跑几轮，整个任务反而可能更贵。

他们做的改动其实都很细。精简 Prompt、低频工具按需加载、优化缓存布局、减少冗余行号，再调整 Subagent 和模型分工。

每一项省得不多，叠起来就是 7%。

这也让我觉得 Agent 真正规模化以后，Harness 本身就是成本控制系统。

Context 怎么塞、缓存怎么命中、工具什么时候加载、任务交给哪个模型，这些工程细节最后都会直接变成钱。
调用量越大，这种差距越明显。
author: Xudong07452910
quoted_text:
here's a prompt to improve your agent harness based on what we've learned at cursor. enjoy

# Improve this agent harness's token efficiency

You're working on an LLM agent harness: the system prompt, tool definitions, request assembly, context caching, compaction, and retrieval, and how work is split across agents. Make the agent's runs cheaper without making it worse at its job.

- Objective: lower price-weighted token cost per completed task.
- Constraint: no measurable drop in task quality.

Measure per task, not per request. Every turn resends the prefix (tools, instructions, setup, and the conversation so far), so a change that shrinks each request but adds turns can cost more. Weight tokens by billing type: output, uncached input, and cached input are priced very differently.

Work in this order: map the harness and measure the baseline, rank the opportunities, make the changes that are safe to make directly, put the rest behind flags or in proposals, then report.

Figures below come from one team's production coding agent and its multi-agent experiments. Use them to gauge magnitude, not as targets. One round of these changes (prompt trimming, tool offloading, cache layout, sparse line numbers, subagent tuning) cut that team's overall token cost about 7% with no loss in quality. The larger percentages apply only to the part of the request each change touched.

## Principles

1. Change what the harness sends, not how hard the model tries. Don't ask the model to conserve tokens. A harness that told its model to "take care to preserve tokens and not be wasteful" found it grew reluctant to take on ambitious tasks and sometimes quit, saying it wasn't supposed to waste tokens.
2. Capable models need definitions, not commands. Lists of "DO NOT", "You must", and "Important", and guards against older models' habits, can usually be replaced with plain descriptions of what each tool does. One team cut about two-thirds of its system prompt this way, and the shorter prompt worked across model families. Instruct only on what the model can't know (the product, the environment, the user's processes) and on quirks you've seen in transcripts.
3. Static context is for what most turns need. Everything else should be discoverable when needed. Less up-front context also means less confusing or contradictory information.
4. Expect removals to win. Guardrails written for weaker models, coordination steps that became bottlenecks, and prompting for behavior the model now does on its own all cost tokens.
5. Real usage decides. Evals are a fast proxy, but they skew toward hard problems and miss the real mix of requests.

## 1. Map the harness and measure the baseline

Find:

- Where requests are assembled, the system prompt, and tool schemas. If a framework or SDK builds requests, find its hooks for message order, cache control, and tool loading.
- How tool results are formatted, and how history is kept, trimmed, or summarized.
- How subagents or parallel agents are spawned, if any.
- Which models and provider APIs are used. From the provider's docs, get the prompt caching behavior (automatic or explicit breakpoints, TTL, minimum cacheable length) and the prices for output, uncached input, and cached input.
- Existing logging, token accounting, and evals.

If the harness doesn't record per-request token usage by billing type and cache hits, add that first. Everything later depends on it.

Then render a few real requests (from logs, or by running representative tasks) and count tokens per section with the model's tokenizer or the API's usage fields. Produce:

- Cost share by source × billing type. Sources: system prompt, tool definitions, skill/rule/integration descriptions, user messages, file reads, search results, command and other tool output, history, summaries, subagents.
- Static tokens per request, cache hit rate, and turns per task.
- Per tool: the share of runs that call it at least once, and its error rate.

Read the rendered requests, not just the templates. Duplication, leaked volatile values, and misordered blocks only show up there.

Rank opportunities by share of spend × fraction removable ÷ quality risk.

## 2. System prompt and injected context

Label every instruction:

- Keep: product or environment knowledge the model can't infer, fixes for quirks seen in this model's transcripts, and rules a mode depends on.
- Rewrite: commands and emphasis into plain descriptions. Reminders into constraints: "No TODOs, no partial implementations" works better than "remember to finish implementations." Vague quantities into ranges: "generate 20–100 tasks" gets far more ambitious behavior than "generate many tasks."
- Delete: things capable models do by default, guards against behavior you haven't seen from this model, text that repeats tool descriptions, and lines that could contradict a user request. Models trained to rank system instructions above user messages will side with the system prompt.
- Move: anything per-user or per-request (date, environment, repo state, lists of skills or subagents, user rules) into a user-role setup message after the cache boundary.

Audit other injected context the same way. As models improved, the team behind these figures dropped directory trees, pre-retrieved snippets, compressed copies of attached files, lint errors injected after every edit, forced expansion of short file reads, and caps on tool calls per turn. They kept small, high-value facts: OS, repo status, and open or recently viewed files.

Skip checklists for open-ended work. The model optimizes the listed items and deprioritizes everything else.

## 3. Tool definitions

Tool schemas ride along on every request. Most tools beyond the core set were each needed in under 20% of conversations, and moving them out of static context cut tool-description tokens 60%. Doing the same for integration tools (such as MCP servers), with names in context and full schemas in one folder per server that the agent can search with grep or jq, cut total tokens 46.9% in sessions that used them.

- Keep in static context: high-frequency tools (for a coding agent: read, search, edit, shell), tools the model tries to call even when they're absent, and tools a mode depends on.
- Offload the rest: leave a name or one-line pointer and make the full schema discoverable on demand. Group related tools so they load together, and put status (such as "needs re-authentication") where the agent will see it.
- Tighten what remains: describe behavior and arguments, and drop usage lectures.
- Pick the split by testing a few configurations and tracking tokens, cost, latency, tool-call errors, and task success.

## 4. Cache layout

Order each request so the reusable prefix is as long as possible:

`tool definitions → system instructions → [breakpoint] → setup message (skills, subagents, rules, environment) → [breakpoint] → conversation`

- Keep the prefix byte-identical across turns. Use deterministic tool order and serialization, put timestamps and IDs after the boundary, and don't rewrite earlier messages except when compacting.
- Use explicit breakpoints if the provider supports them. Otherwise rely on automatic prefix caching with the stable part first. Respect TTL and minimum-length rules.
- Switching models mid-conversation throws away the cache (caches are per model and provider) and hands the new model a history it didn't write. When a different model is needed, run it as a subagent with fresh context.

Explicit breakpoints plus moving per-request setup after them cut cold cache misses 20%.

## 5. Tool results and other context added during a run

- Large outputs (commands, integrations, logs): write them to a file and return the path, size, and a short tail. The agent can tail, grep, or read ranges for more. Truncating loses data, and inlining bloats every later request. Treat long-running terminal sessions the same way.
- High-volume formats: look for overhead repeated on every line or item. Numbering every 10th line of a file read instead of every line cut cache-read tokens 1.6% without hurting citation accuracy. Each number costs 3–5 tokens, and agents read tens of thousands of lines per session. Also check repeated absolute paths, verbose JSON keys, ANSI codes, progress bars, and repeated headers.
- Good retrieval saves exploration turns. Adding semantic search alongside grep raised codebase question-answering accuracy 12.5% on average and cut the iterations users needed.
- Tool errors waste tokens and leave confusing debris in context. Classify expected errors (invalid arguments, unexpected environment, provider error, timeout, user abort), treat unknown errors as harness bugs, and track rates per tool and per model. One focused effort along these lines cut unexpected tool errors 10×.

## 6. Long runs: compaction, subagents, and model mix

- Compaction: keep the summarization prompt short and the summary compact, carry forward plan state and remaining tasks, and save the full history to a file the agent can search for details the summary dropped. A model trained to self-summarize from a one-line prompt wrote ~1k-token summaries with half the compaction error of a multi-thousand-token prompt that produced 5k+ token summaries. Untrained models may need more guidance, so test how short you can go. A more expensive summarization model made a negligible difference.
- Scratchpads and running notes: rewrite them instead of appending. For repeated work in one environment, a small agent-maintained notes file with a line budget, loaded at start, is a promising way to shorten later runs.
- Subagents: fresh context keeps the parent lean, but isolation adds coordination cost (duplicate or stale work). If the model already delegates on its own, remove prompting that pushes it to. Have subagents return short handoffs: what was done, findings, concerns, and deviations. A subagent should use a different model only when the user or harness says so.
- Model mix: in large multi-agent runs, workers used at least 69% of tokens, and over 90% in most runs. A frontier planner with cheap workers matched a frontier model doing everything at about one-eighth the cost. Planner choice still changes worker spend. One planner that cost less on its own saw its workers use several times more tokens, and the run cost more overall. Measure the whole tree.
- Routing and reasoning effort: send simple turns to a cheaper model or lower effort, and upgrade only when a stronger model is clearly better. A router built this way matched or beat single frontier models on user satisfaction at 41–68% lower cost.
- Reasoning continuity: if the API returns reasoning items (including encrypted ones), pass them back on later turns and alert when they go missing. Dropping them cost one reasoning model 30% on a coding benchmark, and it burned tokens reconstructing its plan.

## 7. Fit the harness to each model

Adapt to what each model was trained on instead of forcing one shape on all of them. If you've tuned the harness for a similar model, start from that version.

- Edit format: use the one the model was trained on (for example, patch-style or search-and-replace). An unfamiliar format costs extra reasoning tokens and causes more mistakes.
- Shell or tools: shell-first models fall back to `cat` or inline scripts. Name tools after their shell equivalents (such as `rg`), and if needed add: "If a tool exists for an action, prefer to use the tool instead of shell commands (e.g. read_file over `cat`)."
- Literalness: some model families follow instructions literally and others tolerate imprecision. Some spiral on emphasized wording. Strip caps and emphasis for literal models.
- Triggers: some models ignore a tool until told when to use it. A literal trigger works: "After substantive edits, use the <lint tool> to check recently edited files for linter errors. If you've introduced any, fix them if you can easily figure out how."
- Progress updates: if a model reports progress through reasoning summaries, keep them to 1–2 sentences that note new findings or a change of tactic, and remove instructions about messaging mid-turn.
- Quirks worth a targeted line: hedging or refusing as context fills ("context anxiety"), declaring completion early, stopping to ask permission, and calling tools that don't exist.

Tie each added instruction to the transcript behavior it fixes. Re-audit when models change, since guidance one version needed can be dead weight for the next.

## 8. Validate

- Offline: run a fixed set of realistic tasks before and after, ideally drawn from real usage and phrased the way users actually write (short and ambiguous). Compare task success, tokens, cost per task, turns, and tool errors. Don't ship a change that lowers success.
- Online, if you have users: A/B test each change or small bundle. The primary metric is cost per completed task. Guardrails are task success signals, tool-call errors, latency, turns per task, and cache hit rate. For a coding agent, a good success signal is how much agent-written code survives over time. In general, check whether the user's next message moves on or reports a problem.
- Ship only when cost drops and no guardrail regresses beyond noise. Record null results.

## What to change directly and what to propose

- Change directly, each in its own revertible commit: token and cache telemetry, deterministic serialization and tool order, moving volatile content out of the cached prefix, explicit cache breakpoints, writing large outputs to files instead of truncating, passing back reasoning items that are being dropped, and fixes for recurring tool errors.
- Change behind a flag so it can be tested: system prompt edits, tool offloading, output format changes, compaction changes, and subagent prompting.
- Propose only: changes to which models run, routing, reasoning-effort defaults, or how work is split across agents.

## Traps

- Asking the model to use fewer tokens or do less.
- Truncating tool output.
- Dropping reasoning items to save input tokens.
- Volatile content in the cached prefix, or tool order that changes between requests.
- Offloading a tool the model needs on the first turn or tries to call when it's missing.
- Emphasis-heavy prompts (MUST, NEVER, IMPORTANT, all caps), especially with literal models.
- Forcing a terser output format than the model was trained on. Fewer output tokens can mean less thinking and worse results.
- Optimizing raw token counts instead of cost, per request instead of per task, or evals instead of real usage.
- Switching models mid-conversation to save money.
- Adding coordination layers that become bottlenecks.

## Report back with

1. The harness map and baseline: cost by source × billing type, with the biggest sources called out.
2. A ranked list of changes: layer, what changes, estimated savings and how you estimated them, quality risk, how to validate, and how to roll back.
3. The changes you made, including a system prompt diff with a keep, rewrite, delete, or move reason for each line.
4. A test plan for the flagged changes.
5. Gaps: anything you couldn't find or measure.

text:
I'm joining METR to work on more investigations like our Hugging Face report.

Currently, tons of even basic information about AI development that's highly relevant to catastrophic risk isn't public. I used to be more skeptical of the value of public info, but recent events have changed my mind.

Getting verified information about what's going on inside AI companies seems particularly urgent now. The limited public evidence we have seems consistent with the possibility that imminent recursive self-improvement could massively accelerate capabilities progress, which could then potentially yield extremely superhuman general capabilities within 6 months or a year. If this occurred, there would be a correspondingly large risk of worst-case outcomes. This uncertainty about extreme outcomes could be substantially resolved with more verified public information: we could either build more consensus about near-term risk or learn that such extreme outcomes are less likely in the near term.

Beyond AI capabilities and takeoff, the state of public evidence is also highly limited for alignment, security, control, and risk-relevant internal processes at AI companies. This makes it hard to determine exactly how well or poorly these key areas will go in the near future. (METR plans to focus, at least initially, on just capabilities/takeoff, alignment, and control; I hope other groups cover security, internal processes, and other important areas.)

While I'm no longer working at Redwood, I think the work they are doing is very important; I'm excited about Redwood's ongoing contributions to R&D on technical mitigations and better public interpretation of risk-relevant evidence.

quoted_text:
Introducing P37 Neuro, our open-source robot brain at @OntosWorld.

For a while, we’ve been working on a question:

Can we build a robot brain that keeps working when the body or task changes?

P37 Neuro is part of our answer.

The system is designed to understand the body it controls, interpret the state of the robot and its environment, follow a task or demonstration, and turn that information into physical actions.

A new robot or task shouldn’t always require a completely new model.

P37 has an embodiment layer that represents the robot itself, high- and low-level policies for planning and control, and memory that carries context across actions and failures.

It also supports reinforcement learning, simulation in MuJoCo and Isaac Lab, and a C++ runtime that connects the learned policy to the physical machine.

Around the model, we’ve built the infrastructure for training, evaluation, safety, model releases, fleet feedback, and rollback.

The current software path covers P37-E0 through E6.

We’ve begun testing the ideas behind the system.

A shared model has been trained across different synthetic robot morphologies and evaluated on bodies it had never encountered during training.

We’ve also tested demonstration conditioning on unseen tasks, with no fine-tuning during evaluation.

For the memory tests, we gave the model information before a simulated failure, then compared its performance when that memory was preserved and when it was removed.

text:
I spend a lot of time explaining lending markets. Most conversations begin with supply rates, borrowing costs or collateral factors.

Reading the @BaranosAI white paper took my mind one step earlier: who reviewed the evidence before an asset was approved as collateral?

That decision can affect everyone using the market. Once a wrapped asset is accepted, people can deposit it and borrow against it. 

The protocol is then relying on its bridge, redemption process, price feed and available liquidity especially when markets are under stress.

I think there is a practical future use case for Baranos here: a reviewable risk memo before a collateral listing vote.

Baranos is infrastructure for verifiable AI inference deployed on @fogo. An application can define the model, inputs and rules for a specific AI task.
 Its result can be reproduced, challenged and settled onchain, rather than existing only as an answer from a private API.

Here is where that could help a lending protocol.

Suppose governance is considering a new wrapped asset. Delegates receive an audit, bridge documentation, an oracle plan and a liquidity report. Each document answers part of the risk question, but the important detail may sit across several of them.

The audit describes an administrator’s powers. The bridge documentation says when redemptions may pause. 

The oracle plan explains where the price comes from. The liquidity report estimates how much of the asset can be sold without moving that price sharply.

None of those documents alone can answer, “Should we list it?” That remains a governance decision.

But the protocol can define conditions that demand closer review before a vote. 

For example: a party can pause redemption; an administrator can change a critical contract; the oracle depends on a thin market; or two submitted documents give conflicting accounts of who controls the bridge.

For this proposed integration, the protocol would set those conditions in advance. Baranos could then be used for a bounded assessment of the identified versions of the submitted documents. 

The output would be a structured risk memo: which condition was flagged, which part of the evidence relates to it and whether it needs human review.

I would want that memo published with the governance proposal, where delegates can inspect the underlying documents and challenge the argument before voting.

The Baranos-specific value is that the AI computation behind the memo would also be checkable. The model, inputs and execution rules are committed for the job. 

In its normal Confirmation path, inference runs offchain and a result is posted for settlement. If a valid challenge disputes whether the posted result matches the committed computation, the disputed part can be replayed onchain.

Compare that with dropping the same documents into a private AI API and posting its answer on a governance forum.

 The summary might be excellent. Yet delegates may not know whether the model received the current audit, an older bridge document or different instructions from those used on another listing.

For a decision that adds risk to a shared lending market, I think that difference is worth examining.

I would keep the system’s authority limited. A risk flag should trigger scrutiny, not automatically reject an asset or change collateral settings. 

Risk teams and delegates still need to judge whether the control is acceptable, whether proposed limits are conservative enough and what could happen during a market shock.

It is equally important to keep the job suited to AI. Numeric price thresholds that a smart contract can calculate directly should stay in code. 

The potential use for Baranos is the written material that requires interpretation: audit qualifications, administrator powers, redemption terms and apparent conflicts between disclosures.

Even a perfectly reproduced memo could be wrong. An audit may miss a vulnerability. Reported liquidity may vanish.

 A model may misunderstand a sentence. Baranos can help establish what computation produced the memo; it cannot certify that a wrapped asset will remain safe.

The white paper identifies prediction markets as Baranos’s initial application focus and risk engines as a possible later direction. 

This collateral-review workflow is my proposed future integration, not a feature I am claiming is live today.

The more I think about it, the more this feels like the right place for verifiable AI in DeFi: before the vote, while people can still question the evidence and change the proposal.

If you take part in lending governance, explore the Baranos white paper and check whether your next collateral review has a decision process the community can actually inspect:

Connects an AI assistant to Unreal Engine.

It exposes tools for placing objects, editing materials, working with Blueprints, adjusting lighting, creating particle effects, and controlling cinematic sequences.

A useful starting task: block out one small level, place the camera, and set up the lighting.

This requires Unreal and the repo’s plugin setup.

https://t.co/1dGWbYeSAW

4/ MCP for Unity

Gives your AI tools to work inside the Unity Editor.

It can create scenes and objects, edit C# scripts, manage assets, run tests, and build the project.

That gives you a workflow where the agent can make changes and check them inside the engine.

Useful for turning individual features into a playable prototype.

https://t.co/go63szyvru

5/ Godot MCP

Connects your AI agent to Godot.

It can create scenes, add objects, load sprites, launch the game, and read error messages.

That last part matters. When something breaks, the agent can inspect the actual error and work on a fix.

A good option for building a small game around one clear mechanic.

https://t.co/qXwHTtguqL

6/ MCP for Blender

For creating and changing the 3D objects that go into your game.

Connect it to Blender, then ask your AI to create objects, adjust materials, and arrange scenes.

It also supports asset sources including Poly Haven and Sketchfab, plus optional AI model-generation services.

Think props, buildings, furniture, and environment pieces. Check asset licenses and any external service costs.

https://t.co/n1xKro20HB

7/ Agentic Gamedev Skills

For the work that comes after “the game runs.”

This collection focuses on mini-games, with workflows for testing mechanics, tuning difficulty, adding sound, improving impact feedback, and catching browser crashes.

Useful when your prototype works but jumping feels weak, the rules are confusing, or one cheap trick wins every time.

https://t.co/wx8b2PRU3f

My suggestion: pick one engine, add the relevant skills, and build one small playable level.

Try this prompt:

“Build a five-minute playable demo of [idea]. Use the installed game-development skills and connected tools. Start with movement, camera, one core mechanic, and a clear win or lose condition. Run it and fix errors before adding more features. Then improve lighting, sound, feedback, and performance. Tell me what still needs human testing.”

AAA-quality work still takes art direction, good assets, optimization, and a lot of testing. No repo guarantees that.

But you can start with one room, one enemy, and one mechanic worth playing again.

What game have you wanted to build for years?

text:
When an earthquake hits and the electrical grid dies,
the world learns what a country is really made of.

In New Orleans during Katrina, stores were shot open.
In New York during blackouts, pharmacies were looted clean.
When water supplies run low, bottled water prices jump to twenty dollars.

Now look at Japan when the ground tears open.

The power fails. The cash registers die. The automatic sliding doors freeze shut.
Outside, freezing rain or snow is falling.
The entire town is plunged into absolute blackness.

The twenty-year-old convenience store clerk doesn't run away.
He pulls the glass doors open with his bare hands.
He straps a small LED flashlight around his forehead.

He walks out into the sub-zero chill and sets up a small folding table.

Soon, two hundred shivering residents form a line down the sidewalk.
No screaming. No pushing. No frantic mob rushing the aisles.

They stand in complete silence, one behind the other.

The clerk has written on a piece of cardboard:
"Two rice balls and one bottle of water per person.
We want everyone to eat tonight."

The store has zero electricity to scan barcodes.
So the clerk punches the numbers into a battery-powered calculator by hand.

He doesn't charge ten dollars for water.
He doesn't double the price of bread.
He sells every item at the exact normal retail price: 108 yen.

When people reach into their pockets and pull out soaked bills,
the clerk counts out exact metal change with his frozen fingers.

And watch what the customers do:
Many hand him a 500-yen coin, take their single bottle of water,
and say: "Keep the rest for the next person who doesn't have cash."

They leave.
The store is not trashed. Not a single shelf is looted.

Civilization is not your stock market.
It is not your military budget.

Civilization is what happens in a pitch-black parking lot
when the power is cut,
and nobody forgets who they are.

In a September 28 livestream, Bitget CEO Gracy Chen @GracyBitget said attackers exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a third-party security product to obtain internal credentials. They used those credentials to access wallet backend systems, insert fraudulent withdrawal commands and bypass risk controls, then deleted traces of the transfers. Chen said private keys were not compromised and an inside job had been preliminarily ruled out. Bitget has not identified the attackers and plans to release an incident report.

text:
I don’t think THORChain’s TSS + validator model represents true decentralization.

The selected validators set collectively controls the underlying assets in the TSS vaults. Once the signing threshold is reached, those validators can move the funds. So from a custody perspective, THORChain is not comparable to Bitcoin or Ethereum base-layer consensus — it effectively acts as an intermediary between users and the native chains.

TSS distributes control among multiple parties, but distributing an intermediary does not eliminate the intermediary.

text:
Bitget CEO: Why Withdrawals Were Paused and Restored in Phases

Bitget CEO Gracy Chen @GracyBitget  said during a September 28 livestream that the security incident affected the exchange’s withdrawal infrastructure across multiple chains and assets. As a result, each chain had to undergo a series of security checks before withdrawals could resume, requiring the platform to restore withdrawals in phases. She said the suspension was a security measure and was not related to the sufficiency of user assets, with the related losses fully covered by the Bitget Protection Fund.

Bitget restored BTC withdrawals first because the BTC withdrawal pipeline was the first to be ready and had not been affected by the attack, meaning it did not require the same level of comprehensive security verification. ETH and USDT withdrawals were restored later based on the progress of security checks and user demand.

text:
我现在的重点就是结合自己做的双币来通过期权做组合。

如果小伙伴感兴趣的话，回来我就开放出来，起码是我自己在用，能用，而且好用的我才会开放。

目前还是在测试阶段，但我觉得已经逐渐接近可测试版本了。

主要功能如下：

1. 选择低买 / 高卖、投入金额和天数，自动计算到期日期。

2. 接入中心化交易所双币产品，展示年化、本期收益和目标价，看合适了再选。

3. 接入 Deribit bitcoin:native  期权，展示报价、参考年化、波动率曲线和持仓分布。

4. 自动匹配同方向、同目标价、同到期时间的期权，对比双币和卖期权哪边报价更高。

5. 按实际盘口深度和费用预算，估算卖出期权能收到多少权利金。

6. 测算不同到期价格下的接币成本、卖币价格和盈亏，并与直接持有对比。

7. 提供现金担保卖看跌、持币卖看涨的自建组合测算。

8. 记录双币交易和实际结算结果，支持复盘、导出和备份。

目前以筛选和测算为主，还没有做自动下单功能，但已经可以接入各个交易所的 API 了，目前这个版本我想做的就是：

1. 找到性价比最高的双币投资。

2. 通过期权组合出自己的双币理财，尤其是接入了低价买入的策略，即便是用期权，也可以低价抄底现货。

3. 期权数据的可视化，简易化操作。

大概就是这些。

text:
9月28日—10月4日全球宏观指引：能源价格为轴心，二次加息审判为主叙事！

外交叙事退潮→能源风险反扑→就业与通胀决定美债下一轮方向，中国假期让市场失去部分流动性支撑！

本周宏观逻辑链：

中美峰会落地 ：市场对贸易与科技风险溢价是否重新定价？

美伊继续谈判：能否继续谈判乐观预期，Brent价格波动，决定全球能源通胀预期

美债收益率高位：美国内生通胀多严重？

PCE + ISM + 非农 ：数据组合验证美国增长与通胀情况，10月加息重新定价，债市方向选择以及对全球流动性影响如何？

一，第一主线，中美峰会结束后，双方对本次峰会成果的验证！

上周中美峰会后虽然结构性矛盾并未解除，但是在科技与贸易上出现进展

贸易上，双方贸易休战延长两个月，中美宣布300亿商品削减关税。AI上，双方展开对话，随后有部分媒体报道中方企业考虑采购最新美国芯片。

所以本周需要注意的是，中美峰会前市场给资产带来多少乐观定价，本次峰会结束是否满足市场预期，市场风险偏好如何调整，是超预期上涨，还是低于预期回落，尤其是关乎科技与贸易两个关键板块

截止目前，媒体报道显示对于AI与贸易上都有所推进，接下来看这两条线推进是否顺利

二，第二主线，美伊外交反复，Brent 价格回归100美元，冲击全球资产！

1，本次中美峰会两国对美伊局势初步定调，不能拥有核武器，不能对国际海域收费，这是中美两国的初步共识

2，本次中美峰会期间，我认为是下半年对美伊局势斡旋的最大关键，美伊双方，中国以及其他地区调停国齐聚美国，如果本次斡旋无效，美伊局势可能难度更好。

3，在中美定调基础下，伊朗方面目前明确不拥有核武器，暂时不对海峡收费，并且提出恢复海峡通航的条件，但是该条件被特朗普否定，

4，当然，特朗普周末否定后又表示要在周一与伊朗沟通，而身在联合国的伊朗外长同时表示周二回国，并未有计划与美国代表团会谈

5，双方在明面外交上都展现出矛盾与强硬，我认为这不是坏事，明面沟通否定并不代表私下沟通无法进行，而中美峰会带来的斡旋效果我认为还存在，本周则是一个对斡旋结果的重要考验点！

6，Brent日内反弹2%回归100美元附近，已经连续三周站稳100美元上方，9月累计涨幅17%，此前我讲过Brent 价格对于市场的影响

100美元上方为能源通胀奉献
95-100美元区间风险逐渐解除
90-95美元区间二次加息风险解除
85-90美元区间能源通胀逻辑逆转，通胀逻辑回归经济内生通胀

而目前能源价格回归100美元，加上上周债市高收益率引发内生通胀担忧，目前明显增加加息概率

三，第三主线，能源价格影响下10月加息已经从不确定性进入初步定价！

9月23日美国标普全球升至2021年7月以来新高，同时数据显示企业投入价格升至4年最高点，随后Fed官员开始强调通胀风险刺激10月加息概率走高至60%上方

而截止发文阶段，CME显示10月加息概率高达70%，概率对于市场预期影响：

＜50%，市场处于不确定性阶段
50%-60%，市场开始关注加息风险
＞60%，市场开始主动定价，部分资产开始因为加息进行防御性调整
＞70%，定价从防御进入主动避险，加息定价更加明显
＞80%，接近加息锁定，市场将对10月加息进行充分定价

而目前，周一随着Brent反弹，债市收益率飙升，风险资产明显承压，这就是典型的从防御定价进入加息避险定价的逻辑

四，沃什时代，数据影响大于Fed预期管理，本周8月PCE+9月非农，让市场定价逻辑更加复杂！

a，8月PCE重要性需要额外注意

这份PCE数据的核心不是看过去通胀高不高，而是看美国目前到底处于能源通胀还是内生通胀中

上周能源价格短期回落，但是美债长短利率+PMI数据给出警示，美国通胀已经从能源冲击进入内容通胀反弹阶段，8月份Brent处于87-97美元附近，能源冲击减弱，所以8月PCE将会成为市场观察美国内生通胀情况的重要数据窗口

目前Fed面临一个压力局面：

Brent＞100美元（柴油压力高）→企业成本增加（PMI投入4年高位）→美国商业活动依旧强劲→如果本周核心PCE仍然保持粘性→Fed将会得到一个能源通胀+企业通胀+需求通胀的环境从而增加加息的必要性，大幅提升加息概率

b，非农如果太强会成为第二个给美联储递刀子（加息理由）的因素！

目前多方数据显示机构已经把本周的通胀+就业视为全球最核心的数据组合，这组数据也将会成为继续推高10月加息概率的主要动力

当前市场预期9月非农就业9-10万人，这里我把非农就业分为三挡，带来不同的三种影响：

温和，非农就业5-10万区间，失业率稳定，工资下降，算是最市场最舒服的组合，弱化就业数据本身

过热，非农就业超过10万，工资上涨，失业率稳定甚至下降，就业过热如果加上PCE粘性，必然增加加息概率

突然恶化，非农记忆接近0甚至负增长，失业率上涨，短期10月加息概率下降，2年美债收益率下行，但是随后市场可能会交易经济衰退风险

c，本周PCE+非农就业+Brent 多元化复杂组合，我同样也分为三种不同组合类型

最好组合，PCE下降+就业温和+Brent＜95美元，压制加息概率，风险资产有利

可以接受，PCE下降+就业稳定+Brent95-100美元，虽然风险市场还是承压，但是加息概率止步70%，内生通胀有所改善，对风险市场属于解压

危险组合，PCE上涨+就业强+Brent＞100美元，将会把10月加息概率进一步提高，导致风险资产开始为10加息进行计价或者避险

潜在滞胀 风险组合：PCE上涨+就业下降+Brent＞100美元，滞胀风险对债券与股市是有明显打击的，需要警惕！

五，在我个人观察体系中美债暂时超过能源，风险敞口不断扩大，警惕！

9月24日，除了2年美债，其余美债收益率均超过5%，10年美债超过2007年新高，30年美债超过2004年新高，高利率下市场更加担忧财政赤字以及美债风险！

尤其是上周Brent跌破100美元，但是走势与长债收益率相悖，显然能源与债市逐渐脱轨，如果上周只是偶然现象，那么本周则是重要观察点，如果继续脱轨，意味着内生通胀压力已经刻不容缓

如果后续债市继续与能源脱轨，意味着债市已经开始交易其他预期，例如内生通胀、连续加息、期限溢价需求增加、财政供给以及全球无利率风险重新定价等逻辑，这些交易预期都会对金融市场流动性带来较大冲击

所以，本周2年美债收益率需要重点观察，如果宏观数据公布后压制长短利率，让2年收益率加速上涨，那么两者曲线将会追平，这说明市场进入连续加息预期中，对风险市场有所打压，但是不算大风险

但是，如果继续出现2年、10年、30年美债收益率集体飙升的情况，典型的全曲线收紧，这对于风险资产打压将会是非常致命的，需要警惕！

本阶段总结：

一直关注宏观主线内容的小伙伴可以看出我本周没有再提日元风险，确实在日元加息后日元反而走弱，套利平仓交易风险暂时解除，本周不作为重点观察点

还需要注意的是，本周三之后是中国国庆节假期，股市不开盘，大陆资产缺乏定价与价格发现，对全球资产流动性也有一定影响

9月22日—9月27日全球宏观指引：加息之后！中美峰会接棒央行，全球流动性进入再平衡！

很抱歉，从上周连续的出差飞行，本周的宏观框架拖延至今才有时间整理出来，本周已经过了一半，那么这次的框架就简化一下

上周随着日元也确定加息，基本上全球金融加息共振的宏观周期，而本周，核心主线是中美峰会带来的贸易关系缓和以及中东回归谈判桌的可能性，最直观的就是Brent 价格下跌为全球通胀担忧解压

本周宏观逻辑：

美欧日加息兑现 → 全球无风险利率抬升 → 债市重新定价 → 油价回落 → 通胀压力边际下降 → 中美峰会 → 风险偏好修复 → 资金重新选择风险资产与避险资产

其中，无风险利率抬升+债市重新定价+通胀压力放缓+风险偏好修复都是宏观岸线，不容易被市场察觉但是会在关键节点影响市场的波动性

所以本周核心重点——全球央行主动收紧流动性，但是外交关系能不能让风险溢价会，让风险资产更吸引人？

一，中美峰会

1，本次中方领导人访华前，中美双方深度电话沟通，何立峰与贝森特后再纽约会晤商讨贸易问题，23日中方领导人正式访美，从准备工作可以看出，本次访美并未单纯的外交访问，而是要实质性的解决问题

2，本次核心议题，人工智能，稀土，与贸易等问题，今年5月份特朗普访华之后，中方曾提出“建设性战略稳定关系”，这次中美峰会就要看这个新的中美关系是否可以建立

3，所以本次中美峰会看以下四点

a，现有关税休战是否继续延长
b，稀土与关键矿产能否形成稳定的供应链
c，人工智能是否建立在新的沟通与管控框架下
d，双方是否进一步降低贸易与科技冲突升级概率

这里尤其是要注意AI方面，政治上，中美在人工智能领域处于军备竞赛的竞争关系，但是在商业领域，其实中美在AI方面依旧有深度的融合与交汇

所以本次中美峰会的核心不要期待中美竞争关系结束，而是在有序健康的竞争环境下如何让AI产业的风险最小化

二，人民币成为中美峰会领先指标

1，中美峰会前，美元兑人民币汇率升值到6.695附近，而人民银行则对人民币定价设定为6.748，美元兑人民币的波动可以直接观察此次中美峰会的结果变化

2，如果中美峰会后，美元兑人民币继续下降，人民币同步升值，意味着中美峰会进展乐观，中美关系的风险溢价减弱

3，反之，如果中美峰会之后，美元兑人民币反而加速上涨，人民币贬值，说明此前市场对于中美峰会的乐观预期过头了

三，能源风险真正开始缓解——中东问题逐渐出现转折！

1，这两个月宏观侧主要的一套逻辑就是美伊局势恶化引发能源上涨，导致全球通胀压力提升，从而导致美元加息，全球金融加息共振，无风险利率资产收益率上涨，但是目前能源价格压力下降，算是为市场解压

2，目前局势来看，此次斡旋有中国作为核心背书，加上巴基斯坦与卡塔尔斡旋与沟通，同时借助联合国大会，伊朗与美国在纽约会晤，目前的局势无异于增加了中东地缘乐观预期，并且伊朗已经将海峡恢复通航进行了具象化，提出相关条件，一旦美伊达成一致，能源价格会继续回归下行趋势

3，能源供应上，沙特已经重启了东西能源运输管道，红海能源输出风险减弱，一旦霍尔木兹海峡恢复+红海恢复能源输出，原油价格下跌会相对加速

4，能源价格上，Brent 已经跌破100美元，接下来，跌破95美元，与跌至85美元附近，对于风险市场，对于债市，无异于更加利好，也是为全球通胀解压，从而进一步降低未来加息的可能性

这里注意，95-100美元区间意味着能源风险逐渐解除，90-95美元，二次加息压力减弱，85-90美元，能源通胀逻辑逆转

5，当然，美伊外交重新对话，逐步走向谈判，但是并非代表战争风险完全消失，这是需要额外警惕的问题

四，二次加息概率还在！

1，目前10月加息概率依旧维持在50%以上，目前处于53.1%，概率过半，市场处于不确定性阶段

2，影响是否加息，最直观就是要看接下来9月底到10月初的通胀与就业数据，如果数据进一步恶化，按照沃什的观点来看，10月加息概率还会增加，一旦突破60%将会开始引导市场进行定价

3，如果在此期间，能源价格可以快速回归90美元以下，则可以对冲短期通胀反弹带来的不良效果，毕竟数据代表以前的通胀，能源价格代表未来通胀，只要未来通胀压力减弱，加息必要性就变小

4，所以，后续美联储是否再次加息，不仅要看概率，还要看债市定价，尤其是2年美债收益率

五，题外话，再谈沃什政策

沃什主张弱化前瞻指引，这几次美联储会议也是这么做的，那么后续继续执行这个政策，意味着点阵图、中性利率、前瞻指引的效果都会变弱

同步，后续的CPI PCE 就业，ISM PPI 等数据对市场的影响权重都会扩大，导致市场波动的幅度也会扩大，所以严格意义上沃什时代数据波动风险大于此前的鲍威尔时代

六，日元风险降低+通胀对债市影响问题

上周日元加息后，美日利差并未进一步缩减，套利交易并未继续平仓，流动性没有进一步紧缩，但是后续这条线依旧需要重点观察，因为加息环境下，一旦美日利差导致流动性进一步紧缩，对风险市场影响会非常明显。

通胀与债市的影响，随着Brent 跌破100美元，可以看出美债10年与30年收益率下跌并不明显，如果Brent价格进一步跌至95美元，且2年与10年美债收益率并未下降，意味着 能源与债市的关系脱轨

当能源下降无法有效降低长端利率的时候，意味着市场把能源通胀与美国内生通胀进行了拆分交易，这可能是一个非常危险的组合，当能源下跌无法成为削弱加息的理由时候，继续加息的预期会进一步压制风险市场，同时债市风险也会进一步扩大！

本阶段总结：

本周是一个重要周期观察点，

中美外交关系，决定未来2年中美的贸易，科技，外交姿态等等
美伊地缘冲突，决定未来一段时间能源价格，通胀预期，地缘风险等
能源下跌与债市风险，观察市场对于美国通胀的定价情况，以及未来利率预期导向

text:
Sounds bullshit, but this was real:

I was earning ~50%+ APR on sUSDe using @pendle_fi.

Basically getting paid to leave a limit order to buy YT at a yield I was already happy with.

Here’s how it worked:

- Get USDe from @ethena and stake into sUSDe
- Go to @pendle_fi and place a YT limit order inside the incentivized range
- Keep the order resting and earn $PENDLE maker incentives

This stuff is probably too much effort for 99% of us lol, which is exactly why opportunities like this can exist.

At the time, the maker incentives pushed the APR above 50%.

And the interesting part was the payoff structure:

If nobody filled my order:
I kept earning $PENDLE incentives while the order sat on the book + 5% sUSDe native yield.

If someone filled it:
I bought YT at roughly the ~5% implied yield I was already happy owning.

So the way I looked at it wasn’t really: “Farm 50%+ APR on sUSDe.”

It was more like getting paid to leave a bid on yield.

Obviously this wasn’t literally risk-free.

But from the trade-structure perspective, I liked both outcomes.

And this is also why I’m watching sUSDe yield closely right now.

My read is that Ethena has a pretty strong incentive to keep sUSDe attractive.

Higher yield makes holding and staking USDe more compelling, which can help support USDe supply growth and, indirectly, the broader ENA ecosystem.

I think ~5% is already a strong zone in the current environment.

There are always weird opportunities onchain if you’re willing to actually dig.

每天重度使用各种 AI 就是想实现躺平赚钱，用 AI 自动化代替人脑工作...

整整半年里，Cursor、Codex、CC、OpenClaw、Hermes 甚至 AntiGravity 我都用了...

做开发研究全部都是默认当下最前沿的大模型...

我说的赚钱，主要是指通过自动化交易赚钱，能够长期稳定运行的那种...

纯算法策略、遗传算法策略、实时决策、Agents交易、Agents集群决策甚至人类交易员模拟这些方法我都陆陆续续试过了，大部分都是短期看起来让人兴奋，但长期跑下去就会露馅...

昨晚我和 AI 深度聊了聊现在的困境，它最后承认，如果靠 AI 前沿模型可以在金融市场赚钱，那么所有大模型公司根本就不用融资了...也不用开放订阅收费了...

靠模型自己就可以无限赚钱实现指数级财富增长的时候，人类用户完全就是多余的...

文艺复新的大奖章基金背后就是基于神经网络的某种决策模型，那个是真的赚钱，所以至今这么多年，没人知道他们是如何做到的，所有信息都是严格保密的...

这恰好说明，你能用到的智能，别人也能用到的智能，并不是真正的智能...

至少在市场里，所有人都能用的东西，代表所有人都没有优势...

反正我现在是有点后悔，有种在 AI 交易开发这条路上扛单的感觉...

也许我们还是高估了 AI ，低估了人脑...

text:
Why SOON is In The Right Place for RSI Agents？

OP and Arbitrum built chain factories for humans. SOON is building one for agents.

Look at what the OP Stack and Arbitrum have done.

They turned L2 infrastructure into a factory for chains. Base runs on the OP Stack. 
Robinhood Chain runs on Arbitrum. 
Those chains brought massive value, millions of users, and real revenue back to the stacks that made them possible.

That's the proof: the stack that other chains are built on captures enormous value.

EVM is built for human teams

The EVM L2 model assumes a human organization behind every chain. 
A company decides to launch. It hires a team, runs the infrastructure, bootstraps users, markets the product. Launching a chain is a months-long business decision.

The next wave of onchain activity won't be driven by humans clicking buttons. 
It will be driven by agents, and agents will vastly outnumber human users.

They don't sleep. They transact continuously, in parallel, at machine speed. They interact with each other far more than they interact with us.

That's a fundamentally different load. 
It needs a fundamentally different base layer.

Why SOON sits in exactly the right place for the age of RSI agents?

SOON is an SVM-based L2 stack. Parallel execution and high throughput are built into its core, which is exactly what large-scale agent-to-agent interaction demands.

And we're pushing hard in two directions:

1. Agents launching their own chains. An RSI agent should be able to spin up and operate its own SVM chain as easily as it calls an API.

2. Agents interacting with chains. Trading, paying, and coordinating across chains natively, with no human in the loop.

Where the value goes?

Every chain launched and every transaction driven by agents on SOON infrastructure flows back into $SOON through buybacks and burns. 
The more the agent economy grows, the more $SOON is removed from circulation.

That makes $SOON the growth engine of the entire agent blockchain economy.

Now scale it

OP and Arbitrum nurtured an ecosystem of chains built by human teams, and look how much value that created.

Now imagine the same model when the chain builders are agents. Not dozens of chains. Potentially thousands, each launched, operated, and grown by agents that keep getting better.

That's the opportunity SOON is built for.

text:
Although the $INDEX chart has been trending down recently, I actually think the thing most worth watching over the next few days is that RH’s HOOD Summit is about to begin.

0x56910d4409f3a0c78c64dd8d0545ff0705389870 

The HOOD Summit is happening on September 29–30, and RH has clearly been pushing Tokenized Stocks into a more important position recently. Management has publicly mentioned that Robinhood Chain already has around 200 1:1-backed stock tokens that can be used in DeFi, while Robinhood Crypto just announced that Stock Tokens TVL has reached $150M.

And right before the Summit, the INDEX team showed up and interacted under Robinhood’s official Summit-related post.

I wouldn’t directly interpret this as “Robinhood is going to partner with INDEX.” There isn’t enough evidence to say that right now.

But the timing is definitely worth paying attention to.

Because what INDEX is doing happens to be directly connecting onchain Token trading activity with Tokenized Stocks.

The simplest version of its original model was:

INDEX trading → generates fees → buys stocks → gives them to Holders

Now, this model is starting to expand outward.

INDEX is no longer only processing its own trading fees. It is starting to allow other Tokens to create their own Treasuries, use trading fees to purchase Tokenized Stocks, and then distribute them to their Holders.

I think this is actually a pretty significant change.

Because if INDEX is the only one generating trading volume, then it remains a single project.

But if more and more Tokens on Robinhood Chain start using Index Treasury, then what INDEX earns from may no longer depend on “how much trading activity INDEX itself has,” but potentially on the trading activity of other Tokens across the ecosystem.

That makes me think it is starting to try to capture other people’s trading activity.

Looking further ahead, Blend is also turning stocks and Memes into Baskets, while Longbow is now allowing INDEX to be used as collateral to borrow USDG.

So INDEX is no longer simply the “stock dividend Token” it was at the beginning.

It is gradually connecting several things together:

Token Trading → Fees → Tokenized Stocks → Basket → Collateral

And this is happening right as Robinhood is preparing for the HOOD Summit and continuing to strengthen the Tokenization narrative.

That’s why I think the Summit is the most interesting observation window for this story right now.

If Robinhood continues to push Tokenized Stocks, RWA, onchain trading, or DeFi applications for stock tokens at this Summit, INDEX will naturally receive a wave of Attention.

But what really matters is what happens after the Summit.

Because that’s when we’ll see whether people are actually using the things INDEX has been building recently.

Especially how many other Tokens actually start using Index Treasury, how many stocks are actually distributed, and whether Blend gets real usage.

If these things start reaching meaningful scale, the INDEX story will look completely different from what it is today.

It would no longer simply be:

“INDEX gives stocks to its own Holders.”

It could become:

“An increasing number of Tokens on Robinhood Chain are routing their trading fees through INDEX and converting them into stock assets.”

I think that’s what makes INDEX most worth researching right now.

The HOOD Summit is the immediate catalyst, but what INDEX ultimately needs to prove is whether it can evolve from a Token into a layer of financial infrastructure that other Tokens on Robinhood Chain actually use.

You can search in the search bar: from:cfm_sol index to see my other insights on Index.

$Index 15.87m dyor

0x56910d4409f3a0c78c64dd8d0545ff0705389870

okx wallet:https://t.co/CTIEgDD13t

A protocol on Robinhood Chain for "on-chain index funds." Holding the INDEX token is equivalent to indirectly owning a portfolio composed of real stocks, rather than simply betting on the token price going up

Core focus: a 3% fee is charged when trading INDEX. This money is not burned or used for direct token buybacks. Instead, it goes into a project treasury. Every approximately 15 minutes, the treasury uses this ETH to automatically buy tokenized stocks on Robinhood Chain, such as Apple, Nvidia, Tesla, Microsoft, and others. These are then distributed proportionally to eligible INDEX holders. This creates a closed-loop value generation process where higher trading volume leads to more stocks bought by the treasury, leading to more real assets distributed to you

The project has just been launched recently and is in its early growth stage. The treasury is already continuously accumulating and distributing stock rewards. The token is actively traded on platforms like Uniswap V4, and has recently seen a significant price increase due to the overall popularity of Robinhood Chain. The team and community are driving more integrations. The Robinhood CEO has also publicly encouraged embedding stock tokens into applications, and INDEX aligns perfectly with this direction

Additionally, the project solves the problem for ordinary people who want to gain exposure to US stocks but do not want to open traditional brokerage accounts, deal with time zone restrictions, or face high barriers. Crypto users want to convert their trading activities into long-term, passive holdings of real assets rather than pure speculation. INDEX combines "trading crypto" with "investing in stocks," allowing users to easily achieve diversified exposure similar to a 401k or index fund on-chain, with 24/7 trading and use as DeFi collateral

In simple terms, it converts on-chain trading traffic into real-world asset accumulation. The risk is that the chain is still new and adoption needs to be verified, but the mechanism design is relatively clear and straightforward

The above content is entirely my personal understanding and analysis (dyor). If you have other opinions, feel free to discuss them in the comments

Building with @Bybit_Ins.   
 
Bybit and Franklin Templeton Form Strategic Collaboration to Expand Access to Tokenized Investing

The wider collaboration launches with a new off-exchange collateral program that unlocks trading liquidity for institutional clients, alongside initiatives to bring tokenized wealth and yield-generation strategies to wallet-based investors

SAN MATEO & DUBAI – SEPTEMBER 28, 2026 — Bybit, the world’s second-largest crypto exchange by trading volume, today announced a strategic collaboration with Franklin Templeton, a global investment leader with $1.7 trillion in assets under management and a pioneer in digital asset innovation.

The collaboration’s first initiative allows eligible clients to use tokenized money market fund shares as off-exchange collateral when trading on Bybit. The shares are issued through the Benji Technology Platform, Franklin Templeton's proprietary blockchain-integrated recordkeeping and transfer agency infrastructure.

Eligible investors can now pledge Benji-issued fund shares through ByCustody, an institutional-grade custody platform, to access USDT or USDC trading credit lines on Bybit while the underlying tokenized assets remain held off-exchange in regulated custody. The value is mirrored within Bybit's trading environment, allowing clients to continue earning yield on holdings while supporting their trading activity.

“As institutional adoption of digital assets accelerates, investors increasingly expect the same flexibility, capital efficiency, and risk management standards they are accustomed to in traditional markets,” said Yoyee Wang, Global Head of RWA and TradFi at @Bybit_official. 

“By expanding the range of high-quality collateral available through our off-exchange infrastructure, we are helping clients deploy capital more effectively while maintaining exposure to trusted, regulated investment products.”

I love and respect dhh as much as any other young programmer who is inspired by his love for computers.

But I can't help but imagine that, as a black person, he would not want to see me living in Denmark or the larger Europe, regardless of my contribution to the country.

He would prefer Europe to look like it did in the 80s, or to be as homogeneous as Japan, as he said on the Lex pod.

He mentions having a positive contribution to the society, but after listening to him more, it seems to me that he cares far less about that than about whether the immigrant looks more like him.

That means, even if I contribute to their economy, pay my taxes, raise my family there, and integrate into the culture, he would not really want to see me move there with my immediate black family, because I would be disturbing their homogeneity.

I thought for days about what that actually means. It means no matter what I do, no matter how much I give, the door will always come with an asterisk. "You're welcome, but only if you physically blend in." 

I lived in London and Amsterdam. I contributed positively to their economies, that's why they let me in, in the first place. And I like to think I am well assimilated into the society and culture.

But because I do not look like what Britain looked like 100 years ago, nor does my immediate family, dhh would rather not have me live in Europe, or even marry there!?

By that logic, would you also tell Jude Bellingham he doesn't belong? Or Sir Lewis Hamilton? Or Marcus Rashford, who fed millions of British children during the pandemic when the government wouldn't? If dhh's version of Europe has no room for people who look like them, then what he is really saying is that contribution doesn't matter. Appearance does.

And I get that not everyone assimilates equally, and that it is okay to have standards for who you want in your turf. Every nation has a right to shape its immigration policy. That is not what I am arguing against.

But why do it in a way that clearly shows favour and discrimination in equal measure based on how a person looks? Why not simply judge from person to person, instead of categorizing whole groups and communities?

Europe immensely benefited from Africa and its resources. They went to Africa and laid the entire continent to siege, extracting minerals, labour, and wealth for centuries.

My country is still reeling from those effects to date, having gained independence only about half a century ago.

And yet, merely 50 years later, Europe is so harsh to Africans that they do not want them, even legally, accessing opportunities in Europe?

There is something deeply contradictory about benefiting from a continent for centuries and then shutting its people out when they come seeking the same prosperity your ancestors built on their backs.

Britain has a huge healthcare crisis and a massive shortage of healthcare workers. Guess who is the backbone of that? Immigrants, most of them African and South Asian. They work night shifts, they hold the system together, and they do it quietly.

Isn't it irresponsible to walk into a hospital and say, "I do not like the demographics of this hospital. I would have preferred if it looked like it did in the 80s"?

I used to think people had a problem with illegal immigration. But no, it is not illegal immigration they oppose. They simply do not want immigration from certain parts of the world. God forbid if you are just a good human being from that part of the world yearning for better opportunities.

You can have a PhD, speak the language fluently, pay more in taxes than most locals, and still be told you don't belong, simply because you don't look the part.

Why won't we just vet individuals and give everyone a fair chance? Judge the person, not the group. Character, not colour. Contribution, not complexion. I beleive this is not a radical idea, it is the bare minimum of fairness.

To dhh, please don't block me for asking this 😅, and I really do hope I am wrong and that you clarify this. Would you happily let me and my black family become your neighbours in Copenhagen, if I don't have a problem with assimilation? Do you feel the same about the USA?

I am genuinely asking these questions and I welcome discourse here bc I really do want to believe dhh is a good person and he does not have a problem with people who are not white.

And if the answer is no, then what we are really saying is that there is no amount of effort that makes someone like me acceptable. And that is a huge problem for all of us.

I hope I am wrong.
Kaka.

text:
I don't find ddh argument terrible here, and I think it's respectable and we should allow people to argue these things. 

I have a much bigger problem with casual racism, or generalizations. But I think we should allow people to talk about these things. 

They're sort of the elephant in the room. As a son of a Chinese immigrant in France, and an French immigrant in the US, I've been at the forefront of that from all sides.

My mother asked me yesterday "they asked me if I could teach two women wearing a veil, as they don't want a man to teach them". We had an interesting open discussion about it. 

She was worried that if she agreed, it would be ethically wrong as we should not discriminate against teachers based on their genders.

Obviously we're at the forefront of cultural friction here, between muslim veiled women and good-old-white-french-but-open-minded lady.

The point I made with my mum is that without letting people connect and talk, then that friction will transform into hate. 

The only way is to have the culturally-different people communicate. This is why I was supporting the world cup in Qatar or the US, this is why I was for the olympics in Russia, etc.

Also, I've noticed that if we shame people for asking questions about immigration, about the border, etc. then they turn red (not literally). I say that as an open border guy. Same thing for genders, vaccine, etc.

People have different cultures, even within the US.

I think you should be able to discuss about ANYTHING as long as there's good intent, respect, and empathy.

I think people become hateful if they've always been like that, or due to the crowd effect, or because they were shamed at some point for asking questions to overly-enthusiast activists that are convinced they have the moral high ground.
