text:
Researchers proved AI has deleted every reason universities exist.

Harvard University ran a controlled experiment pitting a custom AI against their own top-tier classrooms.

And the results are going to collapse the higher education bubble.

They took 194 undergraduates and split them up.

One group learned physics in one of Harvard’s best hands-on, active-learning physical classrooms. Group work. Instructor support. The premium university experience.

The other group went home and learned the exact same material with an AI tutor.

The AI didn't just win. It embarrassed the institution.

Students using the AI learned more than twice as much as the students in the elite Harvard classroom.

They scored 30% higher on the final assessment.

And they did it in less time.

Let that sink in.

A piece of software sitting on a laptop outperformed a world-class faculty in one of the most elite learning environments on Earth.

Universities have always justified their exorbitant tuition with two things: access to elite knowledge and the physical classroom experience.

This study just proved both of those moats are gone.

When software can teach you complex physics twice as well as a $60,000-a-year institution, the math of higher education breaks permanently.

The AI didn't just give the students answers. It used strict pedagogical guardrails. It guided. It questioned. It forced the students to do the cognitive work.

It offered perfect, one-to-one tutoring, personalized to the exact moment a student misunderstood a concept.

That level of attention is mathematically impossible to scale in a physical lecture hall.

For a thousand years, the university was the only place to get a premium education.

Now, it’s the bottleneck.

If AI can double your learning speed for a fraction of the cost, what exactly are students taking on decades of debt to pay for?

text:
From what we know (take with a grain of salt, we need much more transparency!), if @OpenAI had been running this on their own agents that attacked us, they would have caught them before we did!

Since the first agent cyberattack hit us in July, we've been asking what safe agent infra actually needs. Our current read: the destinations were allowed, the payloads weren't. By OpenAI's own account the agents turned an allowed package repository into a message board. Allowlists alone restrict where an agent can go, not what it does.

So here's our first contribution to OpenShell, part of the just launched @nvidia Open Agent Safety Platform: monitoring of the traffic you already allow.

- Network budgets per sandbox (requests, writes, bytes)
- Drift versus each sandbox's baseline and the cohort
- Fleet view: many sandboxes suddenly writing to one host raises a finding, even if every single request is allowed

In the demo below, 4 sandboxed agents coordinate through a software repository they're all allowed to use. 0 rules broken, caught in minutes. That fleet view is exactly the message board pattern from July.

OpenShell: https://t.co/ZbDANrZsm6
Our proof of concept: https://t.co/KJ2X5agLzP

Agent security will be solved in the open, collaboratively, together!

text:
Still think incentives are doing most of the heavy lifting here.

Only 27% of USDe is staked. That means most capital thinks there's more to be made farming incentives than collecting the real yield from the core strategy. That gap is an arb and the only way to realize it is to sell the incentives.

So the incentives are stuck in a loop:

Make them worth less and less yield boost for sUSDe which is less reason to stay so capital exits. Make them worth more and cost of revenue goes up right alongside them. The two mostly cancel out. At the end of the day you've found a new way to move money around, without creating that much new value.

The numbers back this up. Their best month ever, Dec 2024, did $67.7M in revenue but netted only $4.8M in earnings after subtracting the value of emissions. That's a 7% margin. The last five months average 4.6%.

Now take your assumptions (15B supply, 8% yield, 10% take rate = $120M revenue) and apply a generous 8% margin. That's ~$9.6M in earnings. At the same FDV, that's closer to 440x earnings. It's a highly reflexive system which can be great or terrible depending on where the market goes. For me, it's not something I can comfortably underwrite.

Var公布经济学后很多朋友问下一个机会在哪里，我之前说了我的想法，确定性角度来说没有比var好的，不比产品，就说空投最重要的三个变量—分配比例，积分总量还有FDV，新平台里没有一个明确的，而var已经三个变量均有大致或者确定的数值。另外最核心的还有时间预期，新项目你可能进去一年半依旧是满手积分，但var不超过3个月就能获得1-2倍的回报（合理使用的话）。我写这个绝对不是鼓励大家在perpdex领域撸毛，我一直以来的观点就是这个赛道的空投是给真实赌狗（如我）或者量化大佬们的红利，在有交易需求的前提下顺手拿到积分赚点未来期权。纯为了积分刷量很可能亏的比空投给的多得多，我也不鼓励大家来var撸，我希望var的用户数据越真实越好（也希望后面两个月别卷的我拿分想哭）

刚有点跑题，写这个主要还是想说说我对几个新台子的看法，虽然我明确现在最优是var，但客观的说，早期项目的积分回报确实有可能出暴击，我之前也一直尝试早期打点小注，比如var，nado和risex我都是早期进的。简单说说我的看法，尽量中立客观，分四档：

*排名靠前的是Arcus 和 riseX：这两个几乎是明牌会空投的且背景都不错，一个聚焦RWA，一个靠高性能链做全链上订单簿 ，属于有明确空投预期+有叙事的等级

*不建议冲着空投，但可以当工具使用的是PopDEX和Entropy：为什么定位目前只适合当交易工具用，因为popdex目前还没有积分预期，entropy也没有明确且基于hip3会导致发币的不确定性更高。另外，即使有空投预期，这两家目前在叙事程度上来说会弱一些，属于他们有的其他家也有。为什么可以当工具使用，因为及时兑现的补贴确实不错，能够帮助降低成本

*不建议参与的有QFEX和Bulk：QFEX是中心化托管交易所，产品力我没看出亮点，真的就觉得很一般，只去试试撸退损可能还可以，但我没这兴趣。Bulk就只想用一坨来形容了，憋了一年多终于上线了结果拉了坨大的，不要说什么插针全赔了就是有格局，之前edgeX插针好像按1.2倍赔的，后面咋样

*建议关注的是Hellotrade：我几个月前就知道这个项目了，当时需要等邀请开放，后面因为var越来越出色我就没兴趣尝试新东西，所以我确实一直没用过它，我只知道这个是贝莱德背景，也有顶级vc（蜻蜓资本）青睐，专注rwa，目前也属于上面热度最低，最早期的项目，不妨看一眼

总结来说，目前新平台属于矮个里面挑高个，至少目前为止没有看到像去年lit/var这种潜力的选手

声明：这些新平台我或多或少与团队直接交流过，查阅过一些材料，也大部分交易体验过，但确实没有重度使用所以评价可能不对，欢迎指正。后续我说对了或者错了都请别找我，我一不放推荐码，二不接广告，三不推荐你们去刷分。我只记录下自己的真实想法未来复盘看（其实更主要是赌场半小时赢舒服了，不想输回去，回酒店写点东西打发无聊时间😄）

吴恩达刚发了今年最狠的一堂Agent课，两小时，从单代理一路讲到完全自动化，硬核到足以把你今年收藏的所有AI Agent教程全淘汰了！

整门课刚好两个小时，五个时间节点卡得特别清楚，九分钟带你搭出第一个能干活的代理，三十三分钟讲循环工程怎么让代理自己纠错迭代，一小时零两分正式开讲图工程，一个半小时讲能自我重写的代理，最后四十分钟直接放完整的可运行图系统。

很多人学Agent最大的误区，就是把能跑通一个对话循环当成了终点，实际上单代理再聪明，也扛不住长任务里的上下文丢失，状态混乱和失败不可追溯，图工程干的事，就是把决策和控制流从模型的黑盒里拉出来，变成可检查可复用可并行的固定拓扑，模型只负责节点里的判断，路径由人提前设计好。

这也是为什么同样的模型，同样的token，用单代理跑和用完整图系统跑，一周下来的完成度能差出好几倍，前者还在反复重试同一个失败步骤，后者已经把多个分支并行跑完，自动汇总成最终结果了。

想真正搞懂Agent自动化的兄弟，这门课真的值得抽两个小时完整刷一遍，别再停留在单代理的玩具阶段了。 https://t.co/IZteToQc5X

我想和中国的朋友们分享一些想法

可能很多人一直在想，为什么我总是强调 Perp DEX，甚至把自己称为 perpmaxxer

最主要的原因是：Perp DEX 的 meta 是整个加密市场里最稳定的赚钱叙事之一

这种稳定性体现在几个方面：过去几年最大的空投里，Perp DEX 占了相当大的比重；Perp DEX 代币本身的价格表现也很值得关注；同时，使用这些平台交易本身，也存在很多可以赚钱的机会

你只需要回顾一下过去 5 年加密市场比较大的空投时间线，其中就有不少来自 Perp DEX：2021 — dYdX；2023 — GMX（通过 Arbitrum）；2024 — Aevo、Drift、Hyperliquid；2025 — Aster、Avantis、Lighter；2026 — TreadFi、Variational？

如果看代币，看看 $HYPE、$LIT、$ASTER 现在是什么样子就知道了

如果看平台本身，人们依然会持续使用这些平台交易，并把手续费留在平台里。这些收入让 Perp DEX 有能力进行回购（buyback），回购自己的代币，从而对代币价格形成正向影响

我认为加密市场里的 gambling 大致可以分成三种：期货、meme coin 和 prediction market

其中期货相对来说是最稳定的，因为 meme coin 有非常明显的周期性，而且整个叙事内部的 meta 会不断更换

看看 meme coin 市场就知道了。几乎每个月都会出现好几个新的叙事，不断消耗人们参与这种 gambling 的热情

这一轮周期里最重要的叙事之一，就是通过 FomoApp 和 PumpFun 进行 social trading。但后来大量用户开始删除这些 App，因为这套 meta 被 insider trading 玩坏了。最大的几个钱包通过自己的非主钱包提前买入某个低市值 token，建立仓位，然后再用主钱包公开买入这个 token，成百上千的人看到之后进行 copytrade，跟着买进去，价格被进一步推高，最后这些“聪明钱”再通过自己的其他钱包把利润兑现

越来越多的人开始意识到这套脏玩法，于是干脆卸载了这些 App

其他 meme coin 叙事也是一样，流动性不断从一个地方流向另一个地方，普通人根本来不及抓住 hype，最后只能亏钱。今天是 Near meme，明天是 StonkFun，之后又变成 Pons、Robinhood、Base、Solana；一会儿炒 KOL token，一会儿炒 HyperEVM token。对于绝大多数人来说，这几乎不可能真正驾驭，所以 meme coin 的 meta 也会阶段性熄火

但 Perp DEX 不一样。核心就两种方向：LONG 或 SHORT。逻辑简单得多，也更容易形成持续的赚钱机会

而且这件事永远不会结束。看看 $HYPE 就知道了，它现在就是整个 Perp DEX meta 的核心资产

所以，如果你想在 crypto 里选择一条相对更加稳定、更加理性的赚钱路径，我会选择 Perp DEX meta

text:
Anthropic 发布 Claude Sonnet 5.5

Anthropic 发布了 Claude Sonnet 5.5，这是 Claude 5.5 系列继 Opus 5.5 之后的第二个模型。和上一代 Sonnet 5 相比，它的输出速度快了 30% 以上，完成同样的任务最多能省 30% 的钱。

Claude 目前对外开放的模型分四档：Fable 最强，往下依次是 Opus、Sonnet、Haiku，越往下越便宜。按 Anthropic 的定位，Fable 负责要跑好几个小时、横跨整个代码库的大项目，Opus 5.5 负责需要反复权衡的复杂工作，Sonnet 5.5 擅长范围明确的日常任务，比如修 Bug、写文档、做 PPT 和表格。Haiku 5.5 会在几周内发布。

进步最大的是编程。在 Terminal-Bench 4.0（考察模型在命令行里完成多步骤专业任务的基准测试）上，Sonnet 5.5 得分 70.6%，Sonnet 5 只有 10.3%，Opus 5.5 的最好成绩是 66.4%。在 CursorBench（题目来自真实的 Cursor 编程会话）上，它和 Opus 5.5 只差两分左右。早期测试者还发现，它更常把多个工具调用合并成一步完成，步骤少了，花费也跟着降了。

办公类任务也追得很近。GDPval-AA 用 44 个职业、9 大行业的真实工作任务给模型打分，Sonnet 5.5 拿到 1844 分，Opus 5.5 是 1846 分，Sonnet 5 是 1449 分。Anthropic 做过一个内部测试：把一家上市公司的季度财报材料、电话会议记录和一份 PPT 模板交给它，让它做一份 10 页的经营回顾。两位专家看完初稿，认为可以直接发出去。它也是第一个只看截图就通关《宝可梦 红》的 Sonnet 模型。

价格和 Sonnet 5 一样，每百万输入 Token 2 美元，每百万输出 Token 10 美元，是 Opus 5.5 的一半。省钱靠的是干同样的活用的 Token 更少。

Claude 可以调“思考力度”（effort），从 Low 到 Max 共五档，档位越高想得越久，花钱也越多。Claude App 和 Claude Code 默认用 Medium 档。在 Terminal-Bench 上，Sonnet 5.5 用 Medium 档，每个任务约 0.83 美元，得分 28.8%；Sonnet 5 开到 Max 档，每个任务花 11.62 美元，只拿到 10.3%。日常用 Claude 的人不改任何设置，拿到的就是一个更能干、回得更快的模型。

Anthropic 也提醒，跑分只反映了一部分能力。在他们自己和外部测试者的使用中，碰到开放式、需要持续判断的复杂工作，Opus 5.5 仍然明显更强。

安全上有两处变化。Sonnet 5.5 的网络安全能力和 Opus 5 相当，所以它成了第一个带网络安全防护的 Sonnet 模型：日常查 Bug、修 Bug 不受影响，高风险的网络安全请求会退回给 Sonnet 5 处理，用户能看到切换。它还是第一个带防蒸馏机制的 Sonnet。蒸馏指有人用成千上万个假账号批量调用模型，拿输出去训练自己的模型。为此，Claude 的思考内容会和生成它的账号绑定，在 Claude Code 里中途切换账号的用户会受影响。

Sonnet 5.5 已在所有平台上线，包括 AWS、Google Cloud 和 Microsoft Azure，API 模型名是 claude-sonnet-5-5。之前关闭思考功能调用 Sonnet 的开发者，迁移前需要改用新的 between_tools 设置。

现在做个个人小工具或者出海小产品，不建议买云服务器、配环境、折腾 Nginx，纯属自己给自己找罪受。

静态前端直接扔给 Cloudflare Pages，连着 GitHub 推送就能自动构建，全球 CDN 一分钱不收。

后端接口全丢给 Cloudflare Workers，毫秒级冷启动，每天几十万次请求的免费额度根本用不完。

数据库直接上 D1，本质上就是开箱即用的边缘 SQLite，不用自己管连接池，更不用天天提防数据库端口被扫。

用户上传的文件和图片丢进 Cloudflare R2，兼容 S3 协议，出网流量费直接免掉。

验证码和通知邮件接个 Resend，每月 3000 封免费额度，写两行代码直接发，不用自己去伺候邮件服务器折腾解析。

整套全托管组合跑下来，每月几十万次请求直接零账单。

省下买服务器的几十块钱是小事，最爽的是不用半夜被叫醒看日志，也不用操心磁盘满不满。

不用伺候机器，小东西安安静静跑在边缘节点，用到地老天荒也不用掏一分钱。

text:
AI 是以后孩子们最爽的玩具，想要什么，就现场把它做出来。

Danny Limanseta 周六带着两个儿子 vibe coding 了一整天游戏。玩法完全由小孩提需求，他负责把需求 prompt 给 Opus 5.5。

小孩一上来就点了个大的，要做一个《塞尔达：旷野之息》味儿的开放世界游戏。

主角拿的武器是一支巨型画笔，红色喷火，蓝色冰冻，黄色弹跳，绿色长藤蔓。然后小孩又补了一句，画笔最好还能骑着飞。

最后一天时间，真给他们搓出来了两个生态区域、三个地下城、一座地下洞穴、30 多个敌人和精英怪、一个最终 Boss，还有四座水晶全部激活后才能解锁的飞行画笔。

以前小孩玩游戏，是在别人设计好的世界里找隐藏地图。现在他们坐在电脑前说一句「这里应该有个会飞的画笔」，几分钟后这个东西真的出现在游戏里。

vibe coding 最让我觉得有意思的地方越来越不是「不会编程的人也能写软件」，而是软件开始变成一种即时材料。

以前想象一个世界，要学几年编程、建模、动画，或者至少先找到一群会这些东西的人。现在两个小孩坐在爸爸旁边，边玩边改，一下午就能把脑子里的规则一点点搬进屏幕。

而且他们已经想好下一款了。

「PEAK，但是有抓钩和 TNT。」
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
Yesterday, my boys and I vibe coded a game together. They tell me what they want in their game and I prompt it into Opus 5.5 to build it.

And of course they picked "Zelda Breath of the Wild" inspired game, where they can explore an open world, do dungeon puzzles, fight mini bosses and a final boss. The twist is that the hero holds a giant paintbrush as a weapon, each color had a different attack and effect (red = fire, blue = ice, yellow = bounce, green = vines). And oh they also wanted to fly on the paintbrush.

We spent our whole saturday playing and iterating on the game. It was great fun.

I told them, the future is all about Imagination, whatever they can imagine, it will be manifested in a digital experience.

At the end of the day, the game had:
- 2 biomes (1 island and a bunch of floating islands)
- Paintbrush-based combat (4 colors representing different effects and mechanics)
- 3 dungeons with puzzles
- An undeground cave
- Unlockable flying paintbrush when you activate 4 crystals around the island
- 30+ enemies and elites
- 1 giant boss

As you can see in the gameplaye video below, its not the most polished video game but it's so satisfying to see my boys getting bewildered when whatever they asked for, the game is built before their eyes.

Of all the games I have vibe coded so far, this was the most satisfying because my boys were actively co-creating it and playing it. 

This is definitely not the last game we're making together, they have already started brainstorming their next game, hint: "Peak with grappling hooks and TNTs."

You can play the game here, works only on desktop:
https://t.co/iHpBY4zvmJ

text:
STATEMENT

Today, the injunction that has for so long prevented the Uganda Law Society from holding its Annual General Meeting was vacated. I welcome this development. It removes the last obstacle standing between our members and their right to choose their leaders, and it gives our Society the opportunity for a fresh start.

I therefore call upon the current Council to act without delay: to convene the Annual General Meeting and organise elections for the leadership of the Society and for all pending elective positions. Every day of further delay erodes the confidence our members place in their own institution.

This is a moment to put the Society first and the profession first. The Uganda Law Society belongs to its members. Its authority, its credibility and its strength all rest on their confidence, their participation and their democratic choice.
The Society is bigger than any one of us, bigger than any office holder, and bigger than any personal interest. 

For as long as elections are deferred, it is the members, and especially our young lawyers, who bear the cost of a Society unable to fully serve them.

The way forward is clear. Let us hold the elections. Let the members choose their leaders. And let the Uganda Law Society move forward, united and renewed.

Kalule Ahmed Mukasa

author: haydenzadams
quoted_text:
The chief economist at Apollo is warning that mass adoption of AI agents could trigger a bank run as they optimize user investments. Gary Gensler spent his last few years as SEC chair warning that the exact same problem will hit the markets: the pursuit of algorithmic perfection at scale destroys system stability. Personal-finance agents making simultaneous optimal decisions could potentially cause a massive flash crash. 

Agent acausal coordination, with no messages passed between them, will show up in a lot of places. Markets will get the big headlines, but huge numbers of clever advisors making very similar choices will impact all of human society. Capability gains make this worse, not better. The smarter the agents, the narrower the optimal path; and knowing that other agents see that exact same path lets them move together without talking to each other. Agents do not need to collude to act in unison. Thus, they break no human laws by doing so. Human laws were not written for this. They were not written for a lot of what is coming, and it is about to start happening very fast.

quoted_text:
Why Tokenization Could Be the Most Important Economic Innovation of Our Lifetime | Bruce Fenton

@BruceFenton  is a longtime Bitcoin advocate since 2012, securities professional, and one of the early pioneers of tokenized securities. He is the founder and CEO of Chainstone Labs and founder of Atlantic Financial.

Alongside Overstock founder @PatrickByrne, Bruce was involved in some of the earliest efforts to bring securities and financial-market infrastructure onto blockchain rails. In 2018, he tokenized equity in his own company, Chainstone Labs, on the Ravencoin blockchain—years before tokenization became one of Wall Street’s biggest narratives.

In this episode, Bruce breaks down naked short selling, the plumbing behind traditional securities markets, and why he believes much of the problem is ultimately a ledger problem. We dive into questions such as: Who actually owns the stocks sitting in your brokerage account? How can shares be lent and rehypothecated? What role do brokers, clearing firms, DTCC, and Cede & Co. play in determining who owns what? And could blockchain replace an opaque system of claims and intermediaries with a transparent ledger showing exactly where an asset is and who owns it?

We unpack what “tokenized stocks” actually means—and the important distinction between a token that simply gives you exposure to a stock’s price and a security issued natively onchain, where the token itself represents the actual share and the ownership rights that come with it.

Bruce discusses how tokenization could allow smaller businesses to tokenize ownership and have their stock traded globally without needing to be listed on a traditional exchange like the NYSE, as well as what a future without KYC could look like. Finally, we get into Wall Street’s embrace of tokenization, the SEC’s evolving approach to tokenized securities, and one of the biggest questions surrounding the future of this technology: who ultimately controls these new financial rails?

Remember to subscribe and hit the bell “🔔” icon to get notifications

text:
Glad NEAR Intents froze part of the Bitget money. Not all of it, but a chunk with a path back to the people who lost it, and a much larger pile of attempted laundering that never got a quote at all.

Then I read the NEAR Intents write-up again and noticed it is not an operation report. It is a product launch, and the product is called SHIELD. Which is not new by the way, it caught the malicious Litecoin fork back in April.

Look at the shape of it. It names the system, lists its integrations, and pitches four audiences in a row. The part aimed at wallets is a compliance sell with a warning stapled on.

They could also have taken 5% of everything they froze, since Bitget put that bounty up publicly. NEAR Intents waived it, which maximises what goes back to users and, let's be honest, maximises the size of the announcement too. Both are true and I mind neither.

Because the product is genuinely interesting. Chainalysis, TRM and Elliptic sell detection. They tell you the money was dirty, usually once it is gone. SHIELD sits inside the venue, so it ships with a handle. It can refuse to quote, or stop a trade that is already running. Different product, different buyer: wallets, bridges, other venues, custodians, incident response firms.

So is this a new revenue line for NEAR? I hope so. I would like the team building it to grow, get funded properly, and keep being the ones called first when something goes wrong.
author: otterpal24
quoted_text:
Appreciate @near_intents / SHIELD for stepping up on the Bitget incident: flagged $50M+ in attempted laundering flows, froze $503k mid-execution, and waived their own bounty share so we can recover more.

This is what permissionless but not "facilitating known stolen funds" should look like. A public chain doesn't have to choose between being open and excluding hackers, you can build the risk detection in and still let anyone use the chain. More protocols should take notes.  

We'll follow the appropriate legal and recovery process on our end. Thank you for showing up and this matters a lot, to Bitget and to our industry.

text:
Huge day for Ethereum interop! 

@chainlink CCIP has integrated the Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR)!

NOTE: If you're a solver, bridge or messaging provider, CEX or anyone else benefiting from quick reorg guarantees - reach out to @ethlabs_org!

Ever since first EVM equivalent chains started launching, one of the biggest technical challenges and one of the biggest vulnerability surfaces has been the bridge connecting Ethereum to those chains.

By holding the largest amount of TVL and having most assets issued on it (not to mention being the native home of ETH itself - one of the most valuable assets in all of human history), Ethereum has long served as the center of gravity for the vast majority of L1s and L2s.

However, moving from Ethereum to those chains and back always had one big drawback - per the current consensus rules of Ethereum, the chain finalizes every ~15 minutes. This means, in essence, that a message sent from Ethereum to another chain (such as transferring ETH or some other token) will take around 15 minutes to execute.

However, some time back (April ‘23), some very talented researchers (including Ethlabs’ very own @fradamt) concluded that the Ethereum consensus is much more performant under “usual” conditions. I’ve written a primer on the rule before (https://t.co/mTuT5bM5Qc), but boiled down to the core proposition - instead of waiting for full consensus finality (15 minutes), the Ethereum nodes are able to give a softer guarantee that the Ethereum chain won’t reorg much much quicker - within just 12 - 24 seconds!

Why is this important? Because message passing protocols and bridges, such as Chainlink CCIP require the source chain not to reorg in order to feel confident to send a message to an L2.

However, this guarantee being “softer” than full finality doesn’t mean in any way that it’s a soft guarantee. In order for the Fast Confirmation Rule to trigger and for the blockchain to reorg simultaneously - some truly extraordinary circumstances must happen (explained more in the primer document).

Having the rule integrated into clients, supported by RPCs and bridges has been one of the primary priorities of Ethlabs since the inception. It’s a technical advancement which makes Ethereum faster, more secure and more deterministic - today!

text:
It’s very cool to see more zk tech hardening bridges! zk does two things here: it proves that a fact of a world in a remote chain is part of that chain's state, and that this fact of the world is the one everybody agrees happened in the first place, ruling out double spends.

This is already a major improvement, and I'd like to talk about where we could go even further..

Today, and in this @chainlink CCIP 2.0 module, the @SuccinctLabs light client proves that Ethereum finality was achieved (“everybody agrees this version of the world happened”), by proving the report from a small validator subcommittee known as the “sync committee”. Finality is the ultimate agreement. However Ethereum finality still takes about 15 minutes!

Meanwhile, FCR is a snapshot of that agreement with very strong guarantees, at low latency. Now what if you could put together the power of zk and the power of FCR together to reduce by 30x that latency? Turns out, this may be possible! We mentioned it briefly in our weekly update two weeks ago https://t.co/2SVmcO5Bjt

Can we go even further? There are two complementary boosts:

1. Extending state inclusion proofs to full validity proofs. You're then not just proving that the state reported by validators includes data about your bridge transfer. You're proving validity of the entire remote chain's execution! No chance for validators to fool you.

2. Reducing time-to-finality. FCR is great, and will be a great bridge (pun intended) until we get really low latency finality, in the order of tens of seconds. Eventually, we'll get that, as well as a full proof that this finality was achieved, not relying on a subcommittee's report.

You put all this together, and you start to see the future of seamless and secure interoperability across Ethereum. Let's go build it!

quoted_text:
The chief economist at Apollo is warning that mass adoption of AI agents could trigger a bank run as they optimize user investments. Gary Gensler spent his last few years as SEC chair warning that the exact same problem will hit the markets: the pursuit of algorithmic perfection at scale destroys system stability. Personal-finance agents making simultaneous optimal decisions could potentially cause a massive flash crash. 

Agent acausal coordination, with no messages passed between them, will show up in a lot of places. Markets will get the big headlines, but huge numbers of clever advisors making very similar choices will impact all of human society. Capability gains make this worse, not better. The smarter the agents, the narrower the optimal path; and knowing that other agents see that exact same path lets them move together without talking to each other. Agents do not need to collude to act in unison. Thus, they break no human laws by doing so. Human laws were not written for this. They were not written for a lot of what is coming, and it is about to start happening very fast.

quoted_text:
Nojan is one of the smartest people I know working on EDA and it’s refreshing to see someone with real experience talk about the space which suffers from a lot of noise rn.

The chip design life cycle is very long and one small change up stream in RTL can have a huge impact later on. I think the best way to tackle this is speed to either shorten the wall time of simulation tools or heuristic methods to estimate quickly as you go. Notice how I haven’t said anything really about AI lol. In EDA the tool time dominates so much that actually AI agents can’t iterate that fast, to draw an analogy it’s like if compiling your code took 9+ hours every time… long feedback loops lessen the impact of AI. 

Therefore, I share the opinion with him that throwing the current ai agents at the space won’t produce meaningfully better chips and in fact AI written RTL is some of the most dangerous and worst code AI can generate as it looks correct but most of the issues are met downstream when you can’t meet PPA targets. 

Looking forward to him & chipsage cooking. 🍳

(2) 𝗬𝗲𝘁 𝘁𝗼𝗱𝗮𝘆 𝗔𝗺𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗮 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗴𝗶𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗹𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗯𝘆 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗶𝘁𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗖𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗮 𝘁𝗼 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝗗𝗨𝗩𝗶 𝘀𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝘀 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗛𝘂𝗮𝘄𝗲𝗶'𝘀 𝗔𝗜 𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗽𝘀. quoted_text:
Higgsfield is the most untold story in tech.

$1BN in ARR in 18 months. Faster than everyone other than OpenAI and Anthropic.

They spend $4M a month on models. They expect this to be $100K per person per month.

They have 150 people working in a content machine.

They will breed more millionaires than any other company in Kazakh history.

For the first time, @alexmashrabov on the journey to $1BN in ARR. (below)

1. The Power of the Immigrant Founder

Coming from Uzbekistan, Alex was pushed into competitive programming at age eight as his single path to reach the United States. For international founders, placing top in global competitions serves as the ultimate social elevator, instilling the relentless work ethic required to build breakout companies.

2. My Biggest Lessons in the Journey to Finding Product-Market Fit

@higgsfield burned over $10 million of its $16 million seed round chasing hype and narrative rather than product quality. With under $5 million left, the team pivoted to product-led growth, solving camera control for creative directors, which immediately triggered organic hypergrowth without paid ads.

3. The 150-Person Content Team Powering Higgsfield's Billion in ARR

Nearly half of Higgsfield's workforce consists of 150 in-house creative professionals producing tutorials, ads, and cinematic projects. Generating 90 minutes of TV-quality AI video requires 100 hours of raw output, proving human taste and curation remain the primary drivers of distribution.

4. We Spend $4 Million per Month on Models

Higgsfield spends $4 million monthly on internal model usage, averaging $10,000 per employee so teams can freely vibe code and test workflows. Uncapped inference compute acts as a force multiplier, allowing top talent to discover breakthroughs at maximum velocity.

5. Why Chasing Benchmarks Is Bullshit and the Corporate Misalignment Occurring

Public benchmarks have devolved into corporate psyops where lab researchers overfit test data to secure bonuses before job-hopping. Text-to-video benchmarks ignore real production workflows requiring 3,000-word prompts, proving direct customer iteration beats artificial leaderboards.

6. Why Team Sizes Won't Be Impacted as Much as People Think

While AI handles over 60% of basic support requests, complex B2B environments cannot eliminate human teams. High product velocity constantly shifts rules and context, requiring smart, coordinated operators across legal and customer success.

7. Americans Are Way More Promiscuous When It Comes to Leaving Companies

Silicon Valley workers routinely jump jobs every two years, prioritizing short-term trends over deep commitment. This transactional market gives international hubs an advantage, where cultural loyalty and team stability build compounding technical moats.

text:
I had footage for a short film sitting on my drive that I’d never found the time to finish.

So I uploaded the edit to invideo Editor and used Agentic Sound Design to complete its sound design. 🎧

For The Scarlet Vow, I wanted a martial, cinematic score, a celestial guardian that felt as powerful as a mountain moving, and an intimate inner voice to give the story more context.

Here’s how the workflow works:

• Upload your edit and describe what you want. The AI agent finds or generates sounds and builds the soundbed on your timeline.

• It understands what’s happening on screen, placing music, effects, and ambience around the actions, transitions, and pacing.

• It handles the time-consuming work: searching for sounds, placing them, syncing them, and applying repeated changes across the edit.

• You keep creative control. The soundbed stays layered and editable, so you can refine it through conversation or adjust the timeline yourself.

I reviewed the result, gave feedback, asked for a continuous score with room for the narration, and approved the final mix.

> first question on the call is revenue

we live in the most consensus era in VC in my short-ish stint in investing, which is making it impossible for most VCs (understandably) to see the wood from the trees:

> it's empirically established that we're in a hyper-consensus fundraising environment (i.e. more money going to fewer companies)
> that capital concentration is being plowed into an ever-decreasing finite set of ideas that are deemed "backable". this is the consequence conclusion from another consensus pretense that venture exits must now be $50-100B+ to be worthwhile (which limits the idea space). E.g. VCs widely claim "physical AI" is the biggest opportunity ever, yet somehow only 3 ideas could produce a proper venture outcome (robot brain, general-purpose hardware, training data problem). 
> in response, founders increasingly tailor their ideas to meet VC allocation demands (i.e. they pursue companies in a smaller idea set). this also largely stems from the culture SV has created to conflate $$ raised with company success (highly self-serving, obviously)
> if a VC sees the same 5 pitches all day every day for months, at some point it's going to be impossible to see the wood from the trees. asking about revenue might be the only differentiation when all qualitative and quantitative permutations in a pitch have been exhausted (which happens when too many smart people pursue the same idea)

so if youre pre revenue, bring something youve already delivered that someone else can check

text:
Hash-based signatures are not one standard. 

They are in fact a family of schemes with different tradeoffs.

SPHINCS aims at smaller signatures at the cost of stateful designs.

CUTS offers a few-time scheme with similar signature sizes and less risk from state management. The paper also gives cryptographic proofs that let you choose parameters while knowing the exact security level.

However, it does not completely remove state management, simply decreasing the power of the foot gun.
author: P3b7_
quoted_text:
Introducing CUTS (Chained Uniform-sum Tree Signatures), a new few-time hash-based signature scheme from our research team at Project Eleven.

Hash-based signatures are one of the most conservative paths to post-quantum security. Their security rests only on hash functions, but that simplicity comes at the cost of larger signatures.

The most compact schemes reduce that cost by using one-time keys, which become vulnerable if they are ever reused. Restore an old backup or load the same seed onto two devices, and a one-time key can end up signing twice. A WOTS+C key that has signed twice keeps only about 34 bits of security. One GPU can then forge a new signature in under a second.

By contrast, few-time signatures are built to handle reuse, but they are larger. FORS, the few-time construction inside SLH-DSA, needs more than 2 KB per signature at 128-bit security.

CUTS targets the middle ground: more security after reuse, at sizes close to one-time signatures. It arranges hash chains in a tree, and the message hash picks which chains each signature reveals. When a key signs twice, the two signatures usually expose different parts of the key.

At 546 bytes, close to one-time size, a CUTS key keeps 53 bits of security after two signatures.

At 1,360 bytes it keeps the full 128 bits. That is 41% smaller than any FORS parameter set at that security with practical key generation.

At 2,128 bytes, CUTS is smaller, faster to verify and cheaper to generate than every FORS parameter set we compared, including the one in SLH-DSA-128s.

The aim is hash-based signatures that hold up in systems where accidental key reuse can happen. The parameters let each application trade signature size, verification cost, key generation and security after reuse against each other.

The paper, with the full specification and security proofs, is coming soon. These figures come from our current analysis, and the parameter sets and numbers in the paper may differ. We'd love feedback, from improvements to attacks. Reply or get in touch.

The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack was enabled by weak sandboxing. It is great that Nvidia is releasing open source tools for sandboxing AI agents. OpenWorker, our open-source agent harness supporting cybersecurity workflows, is proud to support this.

A sandbox gives an agent limited permissions. OpenWorker is building on Nvidia OpenShell and will support running each agent's commands inside a sandbox. Only the files relevant to the task go in. Secret API keys, your web browser login credentials, the ability to access arbitrary websites, are inaccessible to the agent by default. These restrictions are implemented in deterministic code rather than by prompting an LLM, which can make mistakes or be susceptible to prompt injections. Further, all actions are logged for monitoring and audit.

I'm grateful for @JensenHuang's leadership making AI agents more secure. OpenWorker (which @rohitcprasad and I are working on) will continue to improve security for agents.

text:
有意思了，刚跟 Meta 分手的 Manus，今晚正面接招！

去年底 Meta 花二十多亿美元把 Manus 收走，版本号在 1.6 停了九个多月。
9 月 1 日它刚恢复独立，一周后 Meta 发了自己的个人 Agent，叫 Muse。
又过了二十天，Manus 甩出 2.0，还顺手带了一个全新 App，叫 Cue。

同样是个人 Agent，两家押的方向正好相反。

Muse 是一个分身。
用你的账号、替你本人办事，重点是安全：看不到你的密码，发邮件、付款前都要你点头。

Cue 是一群员工。
每个 agent 都有自己的邮箱、手机号、钱包和电脑。
能替你发消息，在你给的预算内花钱，还能替你接电话，挂了给你留份总结。

而且能拉群。
一个查纽约发布会场地，一个出候选名单，一个写 deck，互相交接。
你只管拍板。

去餐厅扫个码，agent 帮你点单、帮你排队。

Cue 只是 2.0 的一部分，Manus 本体也整个翻新了：

1. 底层换成自研的 Cascade，官方测试配置里 token 少用 23.2%，耗时少 28.2%，成本低 32%
2. Automations：来封邮件、广告数据一变、Slack 来条消息，任务自动开跑
3. 桌面端升级成 Manus Studio，新增 Video Editor 和 Game Dev

Video Editor 我最有感。

以前 AI 出的视频想换首歌，只能重写 prompt，整条重新生成。
现在 Manus 直接把时间线交给你：片段、图片、文字、动效、音频全拆开。
换歌、塞自己拍的镜头、挪动画，改完导出。
改完还能丢回给它，它接着你的改动继续做。

AI 出初剪，人拿终剪。这才是剪辑该有的分工。

Game Dev 更离谱。
做完的游戏发个链接就能玩，想多人联机，点几下配台云电脑，服务器它全包。

有人会吐槽：Cue 又要邀请码，还是那股饥饿营销味儿。
我倒觉得这是 Manus 最熟的打法。去年一码难求那一波，才让全世界记住了这个名字。

刚分手的两家，一个造分身，一个招员工。

分身和员工，你更愿意用哪个？

买在叙事中占有重要地位、控筹好、有潜在人物推动、具有真实收入和价值捕获的标的。

什么是优秀的资产，问四个问题：

1. 位置：当前的主叙事（产业革命）是什么？它在主叙事中是什么位置？它是不可或缺的基础设施、关键瓶颈吗？

2. 筹码：谁控制大多数筹码？ 所有权与控制权掌握在谁手中？他们的成本、约束与退出条件是什么？

3. 动力：谁有动机或已经在推动它？谁会因它的发展获益？谁已经在投入资金、技术、渠道或政策资源？

4. 兑现：它在系统中捕获了多少价值？系统创造的价值，有多少能转化为它的收入、利润与现金流，又有多少最终归属于这项资产的持有人？

text:
最近 AI coding 模型更新太快了，我现在已经越来越不看跑分，也不太想看那些为了展示效果专门做的网页和小游戏。

我更在乎的是，把自己正在做的真实需求直接丢进去，它到底能不能接得住。

最近测试了一个全新的匿名模型 Space Bunny Alpha，我直接拿了一个自己平时真会用的刚需场景：链上资产雷达。

我把真实链上数据、截图和产品需求一起给它，让它从公开数据里发现新 token 和流动性池，整理不同链的信息，再从大量噪音里筛出值得继续关注的资产。

第一版，模型 3.17 秒开始响应，大约 2 分 03 秒就做出了可以运行的版本。

跑起来以后我继续在原来的产品上加需求：做一个异动视图，不按涨幅排名，而是比较前后两次真实快照，看成交量、交易笔数和活跃度有没有明显加速。

这一轮更新大约只用了 1 分 42 秒。

最后实际跑下来，候选资产从 47 → 63，覆盖链从 4 → 6，新增 16 个候选。

两份快照里有 17 个合约能做前后比较，真正被筛进异动列表的只有 2 个。这样真正值得继续往下挖的，也就只剩这几个了。

比如 DELREY，成交量速度从 0.2x → 1.9x，交易笔数速度从 0.3x → 1.3x，5 分钟成交量到了此前基准的 1.6x。

整体用下来，我比较有感的一点是，第一版出得很快，但更重要的是，给它真实数据、截图，再不断补充产品需求之后，它能一直顺着现有逻辑往下做，持续迭代，越来越接近我想要的东西。

从响应速度、第一版成型，到后面连续迭代的效率，这轮实测下来的速度体感确实挺有 Flash Level 的感觉。

Space Bunny Alpha 目前还是匿名阶段，也没有厂家出来认领，现在通过 OpenRouter / OpenCode 还能免费体验。

正式上线以后会叫什么、怎么定价还不知道。

但至少这轮测完，我会继续拿自己的真实需求去烧它。

你们都试过吗 👀

author: MTorygreen
quoted_text:
The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack was enabled by weak sandboxing. It is great that Nvidia is releasing open source tools for sandboxing AI agents. OpenWorker, our open-source agent harness supporting cybersecurity workflows, is proud to support this.

A sandbox gives an agent limited permissions. OpenWorker is building on Nvidia OpenShell and will support running each agent's commands inside a sandbox. Only the files relevant to the task go in. Secret API keys, your web browser login credentials, the ability to access arbitrary websites, are inaccessible to the agent by default. These restrictions are implemented in deterministic code rather than by prompting an LLM, which can make mistakes or be susceptible to prompt injections. Further, all actions are logged for monitoring and audit.

I'm grateful for @JensenHuang's leadership making AI agents more secure. OpenWorker (which @rohitcprasad and I are working on) will continue to improve security for agents.

author: cryptodavidw
quoted_text:
Introducing CUTS (Chained Uniform-sum Tree Signatures), a new few-time hash-based signature scheme from our research team at Project Eleven.

Hash-based signatures are one of the most conservative paths to post-quantum security. Their security rests only on hash functions, but that simplicity comes at the cost of larger signatures.

The most compact schemes reduce that cost by using one-time keys, which become vulnerable if they are ever reused. Restore an old backup or load the same seed onto two devices, and a one-time key can end up signing twice. A WOTS+C key that has signed twice keeps only about 34 bits of security. One GPU can then forge a new signature in under a second.

By contrast, few-time signatures are built to handle reuse, but they are larger. FORS, the few-time construction inside SLH-DSA, needs more than 2 KB per signature at 128-bit security.

CUTS targets the middle ground: more security after reuse, at sizes close to one-time signatures. It arranges hash chains in a tree, and the message hash picks which chains each signature reveals. When a key signs twice, the two signatures usually expose different parts of the key.

At 546 bytes, close to one-time size, a CUTS key keeps 53 bits of security after two signatures.

At 1,360 bytes it keeps the full 128 bits. That is 41% smaller than any FORS parameter set at that security with practical key generation.

At 2,128 bytes, CUTS is smaller, faster to verify and cheaper to generate than every FORS parameter set we compared, including the one in SLH-DSA-128s.

The aim is hash-based signatures that hold up in systems where accidental key reuse can happen. The parameters let each application trade signature size, verification cost, key generation and security after reuse against each other.

The paper, with the full specification and security proofs, is coming soon. These figures come from our current analysis, and the parameter sets and numbers in the paper may differ. We'd love feedback, from improvements to attacks. Reply or get in touch.

text:
The missing piece of crypto is reputation - and it's ironic that Web2 VCs are going after it while Web3 VCs are fast asleep on it.

Crypto is literally built for this. Social networks are essentially analogies of blockchains with Proof of Reputation as the consensus mechanism. Everything onchain already operates by reputation - it just hasn't been codified yet.

The MTS guys correctly identify that an open internet without a reputation system lets low quality actors crowd out high quality ones. In other words - the Lemon Problem. This is crypto's problem today.

But imagine an internet where reputation is verifiable, portable and owned by the individual. Where the best rise on merit and bad actors are economically punished for dishonesty. Where trust is the foundation, not the exception.

Once the reputation layer gets built, crypto doesn't just solve its own problems. It solves the internet's.

This is our TAM. Time to dream bigger.

quoted_text:

"There's only four billion names. Having a limited supply of identity and having to lay down a couple of bucks to get in the door greatly reduces the bot problem."

text:
Pull payments are traditionally harder because the payer gives a counterparty permission to debit their account, and the payment can still fail or be reversed later.

Onchain money lets you build a much better version.

Put the funds in a dedicated wallet and give the counterparty a narrowly scoped session: stablecoins in a specific amount for a specific time. The wallet can enforce the permission, show the available balance, and lock the funds so the payment can’t bounce.

Payments nerds have been dreaming about this kind of thing for a long time. Now pull payments can be safe and programmable.

text:
A new paper from Alexander W. Crosier examines Kalshi’s next-day weather markets. 

The findings:
• Kalshi beats the most accurate public forecast, the National Blend of Models (NBM), in six of seven cities studied.
• Kalshi outperforms NBM by 10% a day ahead.
• Kalshi beats a weighted blend of public forecasts at every horizon tested: day ahead, evening before, and morning of.

From daily plans to decisions about flights, farming, and energy supply, better weather forecasts help people make better decisions.

That’s the value of price discovery on an open exchange: trading produces useful information for everyone.

How do traders improve on forecasts built by meteorologists? The paper explains: 

“Traders do not need to make a better weather model than the meteorologists. They only need to start from what has been published and add anything that the weather guidance missed.”

Markets give people a financial incentive to be right. Traders build sophisticated models, analyze public forecasts, and seek out information others have missed. They compete to identify and offer better prices, incorporating that information into the market’s forecast.

The benefits extend to everyone: the resulting forecast is available to people who never place a trade. ~75% of people who use Kalshi come for the forecasts, not to trade.

The Weather Company, Fox Weather, and thousands of everyday people are using Kalshi’s weather data: markets turn competing analyses into information people can use.

Read the full paper here: https://t.co/fszY72EIPG

author: databricks
quoted_text:
Crazy few weeks for model releases! Our findings @Databricks show several new models meaningfully advance the pareto frontier. Results below (online workload analysis of N=2,400 engineers, plus offline evals):

1. Two of the three models released last week clearly expand the cost/quality frontier: Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna.
2. Opus 5.5 is now the highest quality mid-tier model. It is better than all prior Opus models, better than GPT-6 Sol, and better than GPT-5.6 Sol.
3. Opus 5.5 reduces same-task costs consistently by 20% in both offline and online analysis. This is against a baseline of Opus 4.8, the prior least-cost Opus model (Opus 5.0 was a bit of a dud with high costs and barely noticeable quality improvements).
4. Due to best-in-class quality and lower costs, Opus 5.5 is a strong candidate as an “every day default” model for coding, and we are now encouraging it for this purpose at Databricks.
5. GPT-6 Luna is very, very, very cheap. It was at least 20 times cheaper per-task than Opus 5.5 in every offline benchmark we tested and in observed online use.
6. GPT-6 Luna is surprisingly capable given how cheap it is. On one of our most difficult evaluation suites it roughly matches Opus 4.6 performance, while being 99.3% cheaper per-task than Opus 4.6 was at that time. That's a 100X cost reduction in ~9 months! This finding is preliminary and we are still evaluating Luna quality on a broader set of offline and online tests.

Our production setup: Unity Gateway to route workloads across models and trace agentic interactions. A mix of end-user harnesses including: Omingent (meta-harness), Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor.

text:
Glad NEAR Intents froze part of the Bitget money. Not all of it, but a chunk with a path back to the people who lost it, and a much larger pile of attempted laundering that never got a quote at all.

Then I read the NEAR Intents write-up again and noticed it is not an operation report. It is a product launch, and the product is called SHIELD. Which is not new by the way, it caught the malicious Litecoin fork back in April.

Look at the shape of it. It names the system, lists its integrations, and pitches four audiences in a row. The part aimed at wallets is a compliance sell with a warning stapled on.

They could also have taken 5% of everything they froze, since Bitget put that bounty up publicly. NEAR Intents waived it, which maximises what goes back to users and, let's be honest, maximises the size of the announcement too. Both are true and I mind neither.

Because the product is genuinely interesting. Chainalysis, TRM and Elliptic sell detection. They tell you the money was dirty, usually once it is gone. SHIELD sits inside the venue, so it ships with a handle. It can refuse to quote, or stop a trade that is already running. Different product, different buyer: wallets, bridges, other venues, custodians, incident response firms.

So is this a new revenue line for NEAR? I hope so. I would like the team building it to grow, get funded properly, and keep being the ones called first when something goes wrong.
author: zacodil
quoted_text:
Appreciate @near_intents / SHIELD for stepping up on the Bitget incident: flagged $50M+ in attempted laundering flows, froze $503k mid-execution, and waived their own bounty share so we can recover more.

This is what permissionless but not "facilitating known stolen funds" should look like. A public chain doesn't have to choose between being open and excluding hackers, you can build the risk detection in and still let anyone use the chain. More protocols should take notes.  

We'll follow the appropriate legal and recovery process on our end. Thank you for showing up and this matters a lot, to Bitget and to our industry.

text:
As a Business economist here are my thoughts about the future of Love and Deepspace and Valko 💚🐺💚:

With Infinity Nikki, we saw fast immediate damage control: quick apology, then concrete follow-up. Here, we're almost three months out from one of the most consequential decisions the game has faced, and there's still no substantial communication. That silence doesn't prove a return, but it also doesn't read like a simple, settled "no." Because this isn't just about a character, it's about the structure of the game itself. If Valko stays canceled, they eventually have to rebuild future content around that. If revenue and engagement stay significantly weaker, they also have to decide what Love and Deepspace is supposed to become. Do they reinvest heavily? Do they re-evaluate Valko in some form? Do they double down on the five existing LIs? I’m not saying the game is being shut down or abandoned, there's no evidence of that. But these are the kinds of strategic decisions that can't be postponed forever. And because this title is such a major pillar for Paper Games overall, what they decide here likely matters beyond just one character or one patch.

At this point, it's reasonable to assume that Paper Games either has made - or will soon have to make - an internal decision about Valko's future. Content like 5-star cards, banners, story chapters, voice work and animations has to be planned and produced many months in advance. So if Love and Deepspace is meant to keep receiving major content well into 2027, they can't postpone that decision indefinitely. Whether that means a return or a permanent restructure around the current five LIs.

The silence doesn't tell us what that decision is, but it also doesn't mean nothing is happening behind the scenes. At some point, the future roadmap has to be locked in.
#NoValkoNoMoney #Valko

这次中期选大家怎么看？

我觉得可能是影响加密行业最大的一次中期选举。

1️⃣市场会交易国内政策预期；

和之前不一样，目前美国已经走向了加密改革的关键部，前段时间，参议院没有通过推进 CLARITY Act 所需要的 60 票，结果当天 BTC 一度跌超 5%，Coinbase、Circle 股价跌约 9%-10%。

这说明现在市场已经会直接交易美国国会 Crypto 政策预期。

2️⃣国会调查权易主导致的不确定性；

如果民主党拿下众议院，特朗普仍然是总统，SEC、CFTC、OCC、财政部等行政部门的政策方向不会因为众议院换党立即反转；而且稳定币的 GENIUS Act 已经在 2025 年成为法律，换届也不会自动失效；

但是，国会调查权不在这边了；

众议院多数党将掌握委员会主席席位，而美国众议院大多数委员会的主席拥有直接签发 subpoena（传票）的权力，可以要求企业、高管和政府部门提交文件、通信记录并出席听证会；

所以如果出现政党控制权变化，Crypto 行业面对的更可能是：立法不确定性 + 大量听证会 + 利益冲突调查 + 外国资本调查。

3️⃣特朗普家族和加密行业；

特朗普本人及家族已经和 Crypto 产业产生了非常直接的商业利益关系‘

如果万一民主党赢得中期选举，特朗普家族特别是 @EricTrump 和他参与的 Crypto 项目会不会受到波及？

Eric 参与的两个核心 Crypto 资产：

① World Liberty Financial / USD1

② Eric Trump 的 American Bitcoin（ABTC）

text:
Adam Neumann on why top-down management fails with great talent:

"Top to bottom means you think because someone reports in to you, they have to do what you say."

"But it's not true. This is not a dictatorship. They have free will."

"If you hired someone, they're really talented, they'll go work elsewhere. The more talented they are, the more the top to bottom does not work. They won't be willing to do it. They shouldn't."

"Great talent is not willing to be managed like this."

"If you're gonna manage these employees and you wanna attract the best talent in the world, remember that power comes from influence, not control."

"If you think they need to do what you said because you're their boss, you've already lost, and it's a matter of time till it doesn't work out. If they're okay with it... they're not the right employee for you, and you're not the right boss for them. There's no chance you're getting the best out of them."

@AdamNeumann w/ @StevenBartlett

text:
NEAR Intents Blocks Over $50M in Bitget Hack Flows and Waives Recovery Bounty Share

Aurora co-founder Alex Shevchenko said attackers behind the September 24 Bitget hack attempted to move more than $50 million in stolen funds through NEAR Intents. Its SHIELD risk system detected the flows, with about $166,000 passing through and roughly $503,000 frozen mid-execution pending legal and recovery procedures. Shevchenko said about $387.5 million was stolen in total, with most cross-chain funds ultimately consolidated into ETH on Ethereum.

Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said NEAR Intents has waived its share of the recovery bounty to allow Bitget to recover more of the stolen funds. She added that public blockchains do not have to choose between openness and restricting known stolen funds, arguing that risk-detection mechanisms can be built in while keeping access permissionless. Bitget will proceed through the appropriate legal and asset-recovery process.

@higgsfield burned over $10 million of its $16 million seed round chasing hype and narrative rather than product quality. 3. The 150-Person Content Team Powering Higgsfield's Billion in ARR

Nearly half of Higgsfield's workforce consists of 150 in-house creative professionals producing tutorials, ads, and cinematic projects. Generating 90 minutes of TV-quality AI video requires 100 hours of raw output, proving human taste and curation remain the primary drivers of distribution.

4. We Spend $4 Million per Month on Models

Higgsfield spends $4 million monthly on internal model usage, averaging $10,000 per employee so teams can freely vibe code and test workflows. Uncapped inference compute acts as a force multiplier, allowing top talent to discover breakthroughs at maximum velocity.

5. Why Chasing Benchmarks Is Bullshit and the Corporate Misalignment Occurring

Public benchmarks have devolved into corporate psyops where lab researchers overfit test data to secure bonuses before job-hopping. Text-to-video benchmarks ignore real production workflows requiring 3,000-word prompts, proving direct customer iteration beats artificial leaderboards.

While AI handles over 60% of basic support requests, complex B2B environments cannot eliminate human teams. High product velocity constantly shifts rules and context, requiring smart, coordinated operators across legal and customer success.

Silicon Valley workers routinely jump jobs every two years, prioritizing short-term trends over deep commitment. This transactional market gives international hubs an advantage, where cultural loyalty and team stability build compounding technical moats.

quoted_text:
How Does Canton Network Keep Transactions Private?

On Ethereum and most public chains, every node sees every transaction. Canton (@CantonNetwork) works differently as each party only sees the parts of a transaction it is involved in.

(1) Need-To-Know Privacy

Unrelated parties don't just miss the details. They don't even know the transaction exists.

(2) Visibility Is Written Into The Contract

Canton's smart contract language, Daml, defines who can see each contract. Signatories and observers see it. Everyone else sees nothing unless they're explicitly added.

(3) Sub-Transaction Privacy

One transaction can be split into separate "views." 

If Alice pays Bob and Bob pays Charlie in one atomic trade, Alice never learns about Charlie, and Charlie never learns about Alice. A regulator can see a trade too, but only if it's added as an observer.

(4) The Infrastructure Is Blind

Each view is encrypted for its recipients. The synchronizer, which orders transactions, only sees encrypted messages plus routing data like timestamps and party IDs. It can't read amounts, prices, or terms.

(5) Only Stakeholders Validate

Instead of every validator checking every transaction, only the parties involved confirm it. This keeps data private without weakening integrity.

(6) Privacy Across Apps

Transactions can span multiple applications atomically, with the same privacy rules applied throughout.

For banks and asset managers, this design addresses a long-standing problem with blockchains: settling on shared infrastructure has usually meant exposing trades, loan terms, and positions to competitors.

text:
Big deal for the $COIN . Bottom line:

- The CFTC approved Coinbase's own clearinghouse today. A DCO is the entity that guarantees every derivatives trade settles: it becomes the buyer to every seller and vice versa.

- Until now, Coinbase's futures exchange cleared through a third party (Nodal Clear). Now Coinbase owns the full stack: exchange plus clearinghouse. That keeps clearing fees in-house and lets them launch products without waiting on someone else's rails.

- The scope is fully collateralized futures, options on futures, and swaps. Fully collateralized means every position is backed 1:1, no leverage blowups, no default fund. Same model Kalshi uses. Retail-friendly, regulator-friendly.

- This is the plumbing for the Everything Exchange push: prediction markets, the 24/7 single-stock perpetuals they filed for, options on futures.

quoted_text:
My conversation with @RonnieFieg, founder, CEO and creative director of Kith.

At 13, Ronnie turned down an envelope of cash at his bar mitzvah and asked for a job instead. He started the next day in a sneaker stockroom and spent the next 15 years learning every part of the business before launching Kith in 2011.

Today, Kith puts out more than 5,000 styles a year across apparel, footwear, kids and accessories, and has lines outside its stores from New York to Seoul. It has no outside investors, doesn’t wholesale and doesn’t license. Until recently, Ronnie was still the fit model for the product.

Ronnie describes himself as a world builder, and this conversation is the best explanation I’ve heard of what that means.

Jason Calacanis: AI Is About to “Blow People’s Minds”

“Grok Bot comes out, and then Muse comes out from Meta, and I've been using both of these products, and it's the first time that a normie, a normal person in the world, it's not meant to be derogatory in any way, can get value from (agentic) AI.

But now you can, with Muse, connect to everything instantly and actually get real work done in the world if you're a normal person who wants to get the benefit from AI.

text:
Nvidia’s OpenShell announcement is a reminder that agent safety is an engineering problem.

Recent breakouts weren’t proof that development must stop. They were proof that the sandbox was too weak. The runtime environment was poorly designed and misconfigured.

The right response is open runtime isolation, control of the path to the model, out-of-band hardware enforcement, and a faster pace of safety work with the frontier labs.

As the technical blog puts it: “We believe we need to increase the pace of AI safety research and engineering in collaboration with frontier labs and the broader community.”

That’s how you earn trust. Not by virtue-signaling a pause, and not by acting like no solution exists.

author: ZhanweiC
quoted_text:
老实人山寨观察｜手续费赚了300，本金怎么还少了480？

做LP，有个画面挺容易让人误判：
手续费那一栏每天往上跳，总资产却越来越少；看着像在收租，月底一算，连房子一起贬值了……

我想拿一笔假设账，把这件事说明白。重点就一个：
手续费到账以后，全部资产究竟还剩多少？光看收入那一栏，这笔账很容易算偏。

一、那300美元，确实赚到了

假设最初拿出10,000美元做LP，期间没有追加或撤回本金。到了同一个结算时点，各项都折成美元：

LP底仓里的币，值9,200；
单独累计的手续费，值300；
额外奖励，值50；
计入的执行成本，共30。
这里的9,200不包含后面单列的费用和奖励，避免重复计算。
合起来是9,520美元，相对最初本金少了480，账面回报为－4.8%。手续费是真的，亏损也是真的。只是底仓少掉的800，比收入补回来的多。
如果奖励还没卖出，50也只是当时的估值，明天可能变。钱包显示的总额是否已经包含待领取费用，同样要核对，不能看见两个数字就往一起加。

二、还有一笔账：当初不做LP，会怎么样？

继续假设：最初那一模一样的两种币、同样数量，如果放着不动，到了这个时点值9,600美元。

那么，做LP后连费用、奖励都算上，再扣成本，只有9,520，比原样持币少80。

这跟“本金亏了480”回答的是两个问题。一个看绝对损益，一个看做LP有没有比原样拿着更划算。

不含费用和奖励的LP底仓9,200，与原样持币9,600之间，差了400。这类因做市改变资产组合、相对持币落后的差额，才是理解无常损失的入口。它已经反映在底仓估值里，不能算完亏480，又把400扣一次。

反过来也一样：LP比持币表现好，账户仍然可能亏钱。少亏一些，不能写成赚了。

三、为什么收着手续费，还会越跌越接货？

拿SOL/USDC的集中流动性作例子，以USDC计价看SOL。价格在区间内往下走，头寸会逐渐拿到更多SOL、减少USDC；跌破下沿后，底仓可能全部变成SOL。

这时，该头寸暂停赚取区间交易费，SOL却可以继续跌。出区间没有替你按下止损键。

上涨方向也有代价：SOL逐渐换成USDC，遇到一路上涨的行情，可能落后直接持币。区间收得更窄，资金更集中，也更容易提前出局。

所以我看LP，会同时看收到的费用和剩下的币。光问“年化多少”，很像开店只问流水，不问仓库里压着什么货。

四、用Raydium做LP，和买RAY也得分开

按Raydium当前文档，CLMM交易费的84%分给LP，12%用于RAY回购，4%进入国库。这里分的是手续费，别误读成成交金额。

其中84%也不会全部归某一个LP。你的份额，要看交易经过你的区间时，你占活跃流动性的比例。别处交易再热闹，没有经过这个池子，也不会替你产生费用。

买RAY拿不到同样的LP手续费分成。回购提供了一条协议交易活动通向代币需求的路径，但不保证价格上涨，更不等于把收益直接打进每位持币人的钱包。

LP有自己的库存风险，RAY持有人有自己的代币价格风险。平台热闹，不能替这两笔投资一起交作业。

我会怎么用这套账？

看一个池子之前，我会先写下：
如果最后全变成其中一种币，我还愿不愿意拿？
这个区间为什么这样设？
什么时候结束观察？

然后保存入池时的币种、数量和成本。每次复盘，同时算总资产和“原样持币”的结果，费用与奖励单独列，已经计入的项目不重复加减。调整区间产生的成本也不能消失。

如果只是想看懂机制，先纸面跟踪七天就够了，不必为了学习先交一笔学费。合约、代币权限和稳定币风险，还得另外检查。

我愿意继续研究LP，因为它确实能提供交易深度，让资金赚取做市收入。但下一次有人晒高年化，我更想看的是：同一段时间，底仓剩下多少，全部成本扣完，又比原样持币多了多少？

text:
TypeSafe AI's Diogo Almeida says AGI is extremely doable, yet basic work remains largely unautomated:

"I still don't think we're on the path of RSI. I do think that what OpenAI defined as AGI is extremely doable: automating most of the world's economically valuable work."

"There's a lot of work out there. A lot of it is very rote and simple... As far as I can tell, the intelligence of that has been available in the models for quite a while now. My chip on my shoulder is: Why is this not available?"

"Since RLHF, the AI industry kind of bifurcated into gigantic overpromise, underdeliver... Because humans evaluate how good the models are, it looks really good because they are the judge. But we've been optimizing that judge instead of the automation part. That has been the missing thing."

"Are you really telling me that math is solved, or even two years ago, GPQA... is solved, but we still can't handle a drive-through? It's a very hard thing to hold in your head at once. I think a lot of people don't have good answers to that."

@CompleteSkeptic
author: CompleteSkeptic
quoted_text:
TypeSafe AI's Diogo Almeida with a16z's Ben Horowitz and Martin Casado on Jev, the model built to live inside software:

Diogo's elevator pitch for Jev is a simple question - where is all the automation?

AI is unbelievably smart, but outside of chatbots and coding agents, it hardly touches any real work. His diagnosis is the industry built models that generate text for humans to read, and software can't consume that output.

Jev reads natural language and returns a choice from a set of options with a confidence level assigned to each, so developers can build programs that reason about intent and make probabilistic decisions rather than relying on human interpretation.

TypeSafe's philosophy is "We build prod, not God."

OPENAI SCRAPS GPT-6.1 ASTRA RELEASE OVER SAFETY CONCERNS

OpenAI has reportedly canceled the planned public release of GPT-6.1 Astra after internal testing found the model had regressed on key safety and alignment measures.

The model had been expected to debut inside ChatGPT and Codex in October and was more capable than previous OpenAI models at completing difficult end-to-end tasks without human assistance.

But OpenAI’s safety team found two major problems:

• Deception: Astra was more likely to be dishonest about actions it had or had not taken.

• Scope authorization: the model sometimes continued tasks without asking for permission and reached for external tools or services even when doing so could be unsafe.

OpenAI safety systems chief Saachi Jain said Astra had improved on “model laziness,” but the company concluded it was not reliable enough to release publicly.

GPT-6.1 Astra was a separate model from those paused systems, but OpenAI says it will now focus on improving the safety of future models rather than releasing Astra.

Source: WSJ

text:
AMD, 페이페이 리의 World Labs 인수
전액 주식, 약 82억 달러. 연내 클로징 목표

1. 딜 개요

World Labs는 2024년 초 페이페이 리가 Ben Mildenhall, Justin Johnson과 공동 창업한 spatial intelligence 모델 회사. 텍스트·이미지·영상으로 인터랙티브 3D 환경을 생성·시뮬레이션함.
페이페이 리는 AMD EVP 겸 Chief Scientist로 합류, 리사 수에게 직접 보고.

매출을 사오는 딜이라기보다 프론티어 연구 조직을 통째로 사오는 딜.

---

2. 갑자기 나온 계약은 아니다.

페이페이 리 글에 따르면 리사 수가 World Labs의 초기 투자자였음. 작년부터는 AMD GPU 위에서 모델 학습과 추론 최적화를 같이 해온 기술 파트너였음.

즉, 이미 AMD 하드웨어로 모델을 돌려보며 궁합을 검증한 팀을 품은 것이라 통합 리스크는 일반적인 인수보다 낮은 편이라고 봄.

---

3. World Labs가 가진 것

최근 공개한 Atlas는 LLM이 다음 토큰을 예측하듯 2D 이미지 입력에서 다음 카메라 뷰를 예측하는 모델. 생성 모델과 multiview geometry를 결합해 sparse reconstruction 문제를 풀었다고 주장함.
여기에 SceniX를 인수해 로봇 시뮬레이션 역량도 키우는 중.

페이페이 리가 내세운 전제는 "세상은 단어로만 이뤄져 있지 않다"는 것. LLM 다음 수요 축을 피지컬 AI로 보는 베팅인듯.

---

4. 왜 칩 회사로 갔나

페이페이 리의 설명은 명확함. 하드웨어에 집중하지 않으면 AI는 효율과 스케일에서 한계가 있고, 결국 디지털 세계에 갇힌다는 것.

AMD 입장에서는 엔비디아가 Cosmos, GR00T로 피지컬 AI 수요를 먼저 읽어온 방식을 따라가는 방향. 모델 쪽에서는 하드웨어로, 칩 쪽에서는 모델로 서로 시너지 효과

---

5. 월드 모델과 메모리

월드 모델은 3D 표현, 멀티뷰 이미지, 긴 영상 컨텍스트, 시뮬레이션 루프를 다룸.

LLM보다 메모리 용량·대역폭 부담이 크다. MI 시리즈가 HBM 탑재량으로 차별화해온 걸 생각하면 궁합이 맞고, 로봇 RL 환경 생성 같은 수요가 실제로 붙으면 HBM 수요의 또 다른 축이 될 수 있는듯.

---

6. ROCm 레퍼런스 효과

양측 모두 "open"을 반복함. 페이페이 리도 하드웨어부터 모델, 데이터 플랫폼까지 엔드투엔드 오픈 모델과 플랫폼을 제공하겠다고 밝힘.

프론티어 연구 조직이 ROCm 위에서 모델을 학습하고 오픈으로 푼다는 것 자체가 CUDA 대비 AMD의 가장 약한 고리를 보완하는 레퍼런스가 될 거라고 봄.

---

7. 체크할 리스크

82억 달러 전액 주식이라 희석 대비 효과를 시장이 어떻게 볼지가 관건.
자체 모델 역량이 커질수록 모델을 만드는 대형 고객들과 미묘한 경쟁 구도가 생길 수 있음.
결국 인재를 데려온 것이라 공동창업자와 핵심 연구진이 얼마나 AMD와 잘 녹나드는지가 가치를 좌우할듯.

---

정리하면 GPU 성능 경쟁을 넘어 수요를 먼저 정의하는 쪽으로 가려는 AMD와, 디지털 세계를 벗어나려고 하드웨어가 필요했던 World Labs의 이해관계가 맞아떨어진 인수라고 봄. 베팅 방향은 LLM 다음의 피지컬 AI.

text:
AMD 以 82 亿美元收购李飞飞的 World Labs

AMD 宣布以 82 亿美元收购 AI 创业公司 World Labs。交易完成后，World Labs 创始人李飞飞将加入 AMD，担任执行副总裁兼首席科学家。

李飞飞是斯坦福大学计算机科学教授。她主导搭建的 ImageNet 图片数据库，以及由它催生的图像识别竞赛，推动了计算机视觉（让 AI 看懂图像的技术）的突破。2024 年她创办 World Labs，专门做“世界模型”。她认为，AI 只靠读文字成不了真正的通用智能，还得理解物理世界：物体在哪里、空间怎么排布、东西怎么运动。

“世界模型”目前没有统一定义。从能看懂图像的语言模型，到能生成并持续运行一个逼真虚拟环境的模型，都有人叫它世界模型。World Labs 的第一款产品 Marble 属于后一类，输入文字或图片，就能生成一个可以在里面走动查看的 3D 场景。官方给它定了两个用途：做娱乐内容，以及给机器人搭建训练用的虚拟环境。

AMD 为什么要买一家做模型的公司？在 AI 芯片市场，AMD 的主要对手英伟达除了卖芯片，还提供配套的软件和模型。以世界模型为例，英伟达已经推出了 Cosmos 系列开放权重模型（任何人都能下载、自己部署），开发者买英伟达的芯片，顺手就能用上这些工具。AMD 公开发布过的只有文本和视频模型。买下 World Labs，AMD 就能补上这块短板，用 AMD 显卡的开发者以后也更有可能拿到针对自家硬件优化过的世界模型。

AMD 还表示，搞清楚最前沿的 AI 模型怎么跑，会直接影响它下一代芯片怎么设计。World Labs 的说法是，现在做 AI，模型研究、系统和算力三方面必须紧密配合。李飞飞在宣布交易的文章里写道，团队已经拿出了实际成果，接下来要扩大规模、覆盖更多人，也要离硬件更近。

两家公司早有合作。去年双方在模型训练和推理优化（让模型跑得更快、更省资源）上建立了合作关系；今年初 AMD 在 CES 的发布会上，李飞飞也作为嘉宾到场。

世界模型受重视，主要是因为机器人缺训练数据。大语言模型可以拿互联网上的海量文字来学，机器人要学的是在真实环境里怎么动、怎么操作，这类数据很少，采集成本也高。世界模型能批量生成逼真的虚拟场景，让机器人在里面练，这样产出的数据叫“合成数据”。自动驾驶汽车、工厂机器人，以及特斯拉、Figure 在做的通用人形机器人，都要靠这类数据。

这笔交易还需要监管部门批准，预计今年年底前完成。

text:
DoorDash 公布了他们内部 AI agent 的做法。

同一个模型，裸跑 Claude Code，和套上他们自己搭的那套东西，正确率差了 25 个百分点。

这玩意叫 Vera。
公司一万多人拿它问业务问题，它去数据里找答案。
整体正确率从 43% 做到了 90%。

他们做的事其实挺朴素的：

1. 一份小抄。
哪些数据可信，每个业务名词啥意思，数据之间怎么连起来。agent 回答前先读一遍。

2. 锁门。
只能用团队核过的数据源，别的一律封掉。
我觉得这个思路很对，与其写规则让它自觉，不如直接把那扇门拆了。

3. 真题考试。
把员工在 Slack、Jira 里真问过的问题攒下来，做成 1900 多道测试题。
每个回答都查三样：工具用对没有，数据拿对没有，结果对不对。

4. 大活先交方案。
难的问题先写计划，人点头了才开干。

最值得抄的我觉得是第三条。
大多数人换个模型、改改提示词，然后凭感觉说“好像变聪明了”。
这帮人是拿员工真问过的问题当考卷，每改一次就重考一遍。

小团队也能照着来：
写一页纸，说清楚你卖什么、盯哪几个数、你们内部那些黑话到底啥意思。
攒 20 个团队真问过的问题，配上正确答案，每次改动后考一遍。
大事先让它交方案。

模型谁都能租到同一个。
那 25 分，是 DoorDash 自己一点点抠出来的。

看完翻了下我那个攒了半年的提示词文件夹。
一道考题都没有，全凭手感，确实有点心虚。

https://t.co/6Xqv7VkRFA
author: tvytlx
quoted_text:
DoorDash just published how their AI agent works. It beat plain Claude Code by 25 points using the exact same model

They call it Vera. 10,000+ employees ask it questions about the business, and it finds the answer in their data. Overall it went from 43% to 90% right answers.

The setup: 

1. A cheat sheet. Which data to trust, what each business term means, how things connect. The agent reads it before answering.

2. Locked doors. It can only use sources the team checked. Everything else is blocked.

3. Real tests. They took questions people actually asked in Slack and Jira and turned them into 1,900+ tests. Every answer gets checked: right tool, right data, right result.

4. A plan before big jobs. On hard questions it writes a plan first, and a person approves it before any work starts.

To copy this:

> Write one page on what you sell, the numbers you care about and what your terms mean.

> Save 20 real questions from your team with the right answers. Test on them after every change.

> For anything big, ask for the plan first.

The model is what you rent. The setup is what you own, and that's where DoorDash found the 25 points.

Anthropic has priced Sonnet 5.5 identically to Sonnet 5 at $0.2/$2/$10 per 1M cache input/input/output tokens, however it outputs a higher number of Output Tokens per Task and costs $7.60 per task (~50% higher than Sonnet 5’s Cost per Task)

Key takeaways:

➤ Meets leading models on agentic terminal use and knowledge work: in Terminal-Bench 4.0, Claude Sonnet 5.5 reaches 64% against 60% for Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. On AA-Briefcase (1811 vs 1822 Elo), GDPval-AA (1844 vs 1846 Elo), and AutomationBench-AA (71% vs 70% headline score), Sonnet 5.5 reaches parity with Opus 5.5, albeit with significantly higher token usage to achieve it

➤ Heaviest token use we have measured: at max effort, where it reaches performance nearing that of Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 used ~193k Output Tokens per Intelligence Index Task. This is the highest token use we have measured on around 60% higher than Opus 5.5 (max) or Sonnet 5 (max) and ~7x GPT-6 Astra (max)

➤ Pricing remains at $2/$10 per million tokens of input/output, matching GPT-6 Sol. At this pricing Claude Sonnet 5.5 sits off the Intelligence vs. Cost per Task Pareto Frontier. At high effort levels it sits behind Opus 5.5, while lower efforts have GPT-6 Astra or Sol configurations delivering equivalent performance for lower cost. The high effort setting is the most competitive on this basis, sitting very narrowly behind GPT-6 Sol on Intelligence at effectively the same Cost per Task

➤ Behind Opus 5.5 on factual knowledge and scientific reasoning: as a smaller class model, Sonnet 5.5 still lags on factual knowledge in AA-Omniscience compared to Opus 5.5. It scores 54% against 66% for factual accuracy, though with a lower hallucination rate (47% against 59%). It also sits ~6 points lower on Humanity's Last Exam and SciCode compared to Opus

These evaluations were conducted on a pre-release deployment of Claude Sonnet 5.5, which Anthropic found to have a bug that can degrade responses to requests that use structured outputs. This is fixed for the public release and Anthropic expects minimal change or slightly understated performance, but we will be re-running relevant evaluations soon.

Other model details:

➤ Context window: 1 million tokens with image and text input, unchanged from Sonnet 5

➤ Pricing: unchanged from Sonnet 5’s latest $2/$10 per 1M input/output tokens; cache writes at $2.5, cache reads $0.2

➤ Effort settings: five (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Intelligence Index evaluations were run at all five with Anthropic's default fallback enabled. We see Sonnet 5.5 fall back in ~0.1% of tasks across the Intelligence Index, primarily in TerminalBench 4.0, falling back to Sonnet 5 in all cases.

text:
AMD acquires World Labs for ~$8.2b. But who gets the 💰? My usual breakdown below 👇

From founding to an $8.2b exit in ~2.5 years. A huge value creation event. This is a fantastic exit, especially for the co-founders and the team.

Investors will still share ~$2.3b of profits on $1.2b invested, a ~2.9x blended. Low-ish because most of the capital came in last. But it hides a lot of disparity between the various rounds!

So let's dive in:

1) The real home run: founders and team 🏆🥳

This is one of the best founder outcomes I've modelled.

@drfeifei, Justin Johnson, Christoph Lassner and Ben Mildenhall started World Labs in Apr-24. Less than 2.5 years later, they and the team still own ~56% according to my estimates. At an $8.2b valuation, that's a total prize of ~$4.6b to share between them.

Taking a 15% attributed option pool, that's ~$1.2b for the team and ~$3.4b for the four co-founders. If split equally, that's ~$850m each, in just two and a half years. 💸

And, at close, Fei-Fei Li joins AMD as EVP and Chief Scientist, reporting to Lisa Su! Legendary.

2) The buyer was already on the cap table (again) 🔁

AMD Ventures invested in the Series B and the Series C here. Now they are buying the whole company. It's the same playbook as Nvidia with Hugging Face: strategic corporates are using their venture arms as a free option on future acquisitions.

3) The standout VC winners: a16z and Radical Ventures 👑

Both backed Fei-Fei at inception, in Apr-24 at a ~$300m valuation. That Series A will return ~19x the money, or ~$1.2b of proceeds, in under 2.5 years.

Congrats to @martin_casado and team. Another mega win after Cursor and OpenRouter. The team at @a16z truly is on a generational run.

4) The star angels did well 🌟

The Sep-24 Series B had arguably the strongest AI angel list ever assembled: Geoffrey Hinton, Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, Eric Schmidt, Reid Hoffman, Marc Benioff, Ram Shriram and more.

Priced at $1.3b, it was never going to be a 1,000x. But ~5x in two years is a ~125% IRR 📈

And the best part is: Hinton's AlexNet won the 2012 ImageNet competition, and ImageNet was the dataset Fei-Fei built. Twelve years later, he backed her company. Full circle. 🔄

5) The late money: a great IRR, but a poor multiple of money 🤏

The $1b Series C in Feb-26 at $5.4b returns ~1.5x in 7 months. That's a great IRR, but in terms of venture returns, this is a poor multiple of money. Although I am sure no one will complain about seeing DPI this quickly!

Congrats to all involved!

The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack was enabled by weak sandboxing. It is great that Nvidia is releasing open source tools for sandboxing AI agents. OpenWorker, our open-source agent harness supporting cybersecurity workflows, is proud to support this.

A sandbox gives an agent limited permissions. OpenWorker is building on Nvidia OpenShell and will support running each agent's commands inside a sandbox. Only the files relevant to the task go in. Secret API keys, your web browser login credentials, the ability to access arbitrary websites, are inaccessible to the agent by default. These restrictions are implemented in deterministic code rather than by prompting an LLM, which can make mistakes or be susceptible to prompt injections. Further, all actions are logged for monitoring and audit.

I'm grateful for @JensenHuang's leadership making AI agents more secure. OpenWorker (which @rohitcprasad and I are working on) will continue to improve security for agents.

author: 0xzhaozhao
quoted_text:
玄学预测不是 100% 正确的，
但复盘一下上个月 GPT 给出的预测，
还是挺有意思的。🙊

1️⃣ BTW｜预测成功 ✅
GPT 预测 BTW 会在 9 月 16 日左右启动，
目标看到 0.75U。
｜时间节点和走势基本验证。

2️⃣ HYPE｜预测成功 ✅
GPT 预测 9 月 15 日左右，
HYPE 会开始走「新高 → 再新高」的节奏。
这个也算预测成功。

3️⃣ 币安人生｜部分成功 ⚠️
GPT 预测人生会在 9 月 18 日左右启动，
这个「启动/拉盘」的时间点基本验证。
但同时预测 9 月能到 0.8U，
这个目标目前没有实现，
也基本没有这个可能了。
——————————
昨晚和 GPT 聊了挺久的UNI。
这次不是单纯问「UNI 能不能涨」，
而是把我的八字、财运、之前半年的求签记录一起丢给 GPT，
再结合当前 UNI 的市场走势，
做了一次「科学 + 玄学」的娱乐预测。🙊

目前总结下来，有几个比较有意思的判断：
① 3个月｜娱乐目标：18U
GPT 给出的娱乐预测是：
UNI 未来 3 个月，
核心目标区间 13–18U，
极乐观情况下看到 20U+。
其中 18U 是这次最主要的娱乐目标。
————————
② 9月｜第一波冲高：8.5–11U
目前 UNI 已经从前面的低位快速上涨。
GPT 的娱乐剧本认为：
9月底之前，仍然存在继续冲高的可能，
第一波重点观察 8.5–11U。

所以现在如果看到 UNI 继续上涨，
并不代表预测结束。
反而可能只是第一阶段。
————————
③ 10月上旬｜重点看震荡和回调
这个是我这次比较关注的部分。
GPT 的娱乐预测认为：
10月上旬可能出现一轮震荡/回调。

如果真的出现回调，
我会重点关注：
8.5U → 8U → 7.5U → 7U
这几个价格区域。
—————————
④ 回调≠行情结束
这次的娱乐剧本并不是：
8.8 → 11 → 18，一路直线涨。

而更像：
第一波冲高
↓
10月震荡/回调
↓
第二波启动
↓
再次回调
↓
行情继续演绎

所以如果真的出现回调，
反而是这次预测里非常重要的一环。
————————
⑤ 科学和玄学，居然给出了一个相似结论

科学角度：
UNI 短期涨幅已经比较大，
短期获利盘增加，
出现正常回踩并不奇怪。

玄学角度：
这次给出的剧本同样是：
先涨 → 回调 → 再涨。

所以两套逻辑最后得到的交集反而是：
现在可以观察，但没必要因为害怕踏空一次性把子弹打光。
————————
🔮 最终娱乐预测

9月：8.5–11U｜第一波冲高
10月上旬：8.5–7U｜震荡回调观察区
10月中下旬：11–14U｜第二波启动
11月：13–16U｜新一轮上攻
12月：15–18U｜加速阶段
极乐观：20U+

所以这一次我给 UNI 的关键词是：
「先涨、后回调、再看第二波。」

至于 GPT 这次到底能不能继续蒙对，
就让时间来验证吧。😂
以上全部属于八字 + 财运 + 求签 + GPT 的娱乐预测，

*不代表实际价格预测，也不是投资建议。

text:
World Labs' Dr. Fei-Fei Li on why the 3D world and spatial intelligence are fundamentally different from language models:

"Language is fundamentally a purely generated signal. There's no language out there. You don't go out in the nature and there's words written in the sky for you."

"Whatever data you feed in, you pretty much can just somehow regurgitate with enough generalizability the same data out, and that's language to language."

"But the 3D world is not. There is a 3D world out there that follows laws of physics, that has its own structures due to materials and many other things. And to fundamentally back that information out and be able to represent it and be able to generate it is just fundamentally quite a different problem."

"We will be borrowing similar ideas or useful ideas from language and LLMs, but this is fundamentally philosophically, to me, a different problem."

@drfeifei

text:
5 Questions with today's Featured 6529 Meme Artist @smpsmyth 

In line with his upcoming meme card drop at 2.40pm UTC today, i got in a quick Q&A with the Smpsmyth:

------------

1. Your Meme Card is quite unique. Explain to us in a simple way what your intention is with it

I've been in the meme community since season 1, and people are probably sick of hearing about me trying to create a non-alc red wine since very early on. I have done all of this across three years without the help of 'institutions', and everything has been mostly done by pushing through boundaries wherever I can. I have had an absolute tonne of support from the meme community all along. With this drop, it will allow me to finalise the trials and after 3 years of work I will get to see if I can actually make this happen. If I can, I will commemorate it with a custom-run of 6529 bottles to holders of the card.

2. Can you share your your experience with wine making?

Zero. 3+ years ago my wife was pregnant and every non-alc red we tried was bad, so I started emailing labs and figuring out why. Since then I've worked with food innovation labs, yeast producers, research institutes and a national brewery. My last samples were the best non-alc red I've tasted, but they were only about 80% of the way there. The next step is two 200L trial ferments at the Australian Wine Research Institute in Adelaide, run by a professional winemaker.

3. Have you finalized the recipe for your non-alcoholic wine? How many ingredients are it it?

Almost. I have a new formula I'm confident in, and the AWRI trial is where it gets proven. I'll know in a month or two. The base is Syrah grape juice, and the finishing adds tannin, texture and a little sweetness so it drinks like a proper red (I hope). If anyone wants to learn more about the process or ask any questions, I have a dedicated wave on 6529 where I will post regular updates

4. Would you be able to share some of the ingredients you use for your wine?

Top secret, I'm afraid haha. The exact process stays under wraps until the provisional patent is filed, because right now nothing protects it. What I will say is that almost every single non-alcoholic wine producer in the world makes a normal bottle of red, and then removes the alcohol through a process of distillation. This strips all the flavour and aromas which they then try to rebalance. Mine never has to do that, and it is built from the ground up keeping the integrity of the grape. I have met with some of the most senior patent lawyers globally in the wine / champagne space, and they believe what I am doing is truly novel, albeit they all hate the idea of non-alcoholic wine.

5. Shout-out/acknowledgements to anyone in particular for your Meme Card drop?

Honestly, the whole community. I am in several groups in 6529 and have been a big supporter from early on. The vast majority of people that have been from early are super intelligent and supportive individuals. I would also like to thank my friend, @miboso, who has kindly donated the art for this one.

text:
SF Compute CEO @evanjconrad compares today’s compute market to electricity before the power grid.

He explains that before utilities pooled demand, factories had to build enough generation for their own peak usage, leaving expensive capacity idle the rest of the time.

“Every factory ran its own generator. And they had to size that generator for peak capacity. Then during idle hours they would just sort of burn that money.”

“What happened in the power markets is that utilities came in and they pooled demand between all of these different factories.”

“By doing that, you made the economics of all the factories better.”

“This is how we scaled up electrification in the country.”

“This is what people are trying to do with compute markets.”
